title: Norske Skog continues data centre development at Saugbrugs and seeks new partner
body:
Norske Skog will continue the development work for an 80-100 MW data centre opportunity at Saugbrugs and will initiate a process to identify a new industrial data centre partner. Norske Skog and Green Mountain will not extend the letter of intent regarding the development of a data centre at Norske Skog Saugbrugs.
With the letter of intent having expired on 31 October, Norske Skog and Green Mountain have agreed not to extend the current cooperation. Norske Skog will continue to explore the opportunity for a data centre at a site that benefits from access to significant power capacity and existing industrial infrastructure. Norske Skog continues to see attractive potential for data centre development and will initiate a process to identify a new industrial data centre partner. The Halden Municipal Council recently adopted the planning programme for a data centre development at areas not used for fibre processing and paper production at Saugbrugs.
"We will continue to explore data centre development at Saugbrugs and start the process of identifying a new partner based on incoming interest from several data centre developers attracted by the revised concept. Together with the investment in PM6 and NND's decommissioning activities, we believe this can contribute to significant investment, industrial activity and long-term value creation in Halden," says Geir Drangsland, CEO of Norske Skog.
This information is considered to include inside information pursuant to the EU Market Abuse Regulation article 7 and is subject to the disclosure requirements pursuant to section 5-12 of the Norwegian Securities Trading Act. This stock exchange announcement was published by Even Lund, Senior Vice President Corporate Finance at Norske Skog ASA, on 1 November 2026 at 20:15 CET.
About Norske Skog
Norske Skog is a producer of packaging paper and publication paper across four mills in Europe. Packaging paper includes testliner and fluting and publication paper includes newsprint and magazine paper. The annual production capacity of packaging paper is 0.8 million tonnes, and the annual production capacity of publication paper is 1.2 million tonnes. Packaging paper and publication paper are sold through sales offices and agents. Norske Skog has approximately 1 650 employees and the parent company, Norske Skog ASA, a public limited liability company, is incorporated in Norway and has its head office in Oslo. The company is listed on Oslo Stock Exchange with the ticker NSKOG.

title: Strong Faroese performance, progress in Scotland and tight market ahead
body:
The Bakkafrost Group delivered a total operational EBIT of DKK 128 million (DKK
22 million) in Q3 2026
(Figures in parenthesis refer to the same period last year unless otherwise
specified)
Strong Faroese biology drove harvest volumes up 24% year-to-date, while FOF more
than doubled operational EBITDA. Scotland's large-smolt strategy shows progress.
The performance in Q3 2026 per region was as follows:
 - Faroe Islands Revenues of DKK 1,436 million (1,405 million)
 Operational EBIT of DKK 267 million (227
million)
 - Scotland Revenues of DKK 245 million (282 million)
 Operational EBIT of DKK -140 million (--205
million)
Commenting on the result, CEO Regin Jacobsen said:
"Bakkafrost continued to deliver strong biological performance in the Faroe
Islands during the third quarter, with good growth and high biomass at sea.
Harvest volumes for the first nine months increased by 24% compared to last
year. While harvesting smaller farming sites contributed to higher unit costs in
the quarter, the underlying biological and operational performance remains
solid.
Our Faroese freshwater operations continue to perform well, with record-high
capacity utilisation. The new Skálavík hatchery is progressing according to
plan, and the first two batches of eggs are performing well. Combined with the
expansion of our broodstock programme, this strengthens our foundation for
further growth and improved efficiency.
The FOF segment delivered particularly strong results, with operational EBITDA
more than doubling compared to last year. Our integrated value chain also
provides flexibility to mitigate increasing marine raw material costs through
sourcing and feed optimisation, supporting our overall cost competitiveness.
Following the increased 2027 quota recommendations for blue whiting, we expect
higher marine raw material sourcing and increased external fishmeal sales in
2027. We also expect feed production to increase to approximately 185,000
tonnes.
In Scotland, we are seeing encouraging signs from our large-smolt strategy, with
these fish demonstrating superior growth and survivability. Nevertheless,
results remain affected by low harvest volumes, smaller harvest weights and high
unit costs. To reduce biological risk, we have decided to discontinue external
smolt sourcing and focus on our own freshwater production. This is possible
because the new facility at Applecross can now supply significantly larger
volume of smolt . At the same time, the continued ramp-up of Applecross is
driving rapid reductions in freshwater production costs as capacity utilisation
increases. These developments are important steps towards a more predictable and
efficient farming operation.
Despite increased global salmon supply, demand has been remarkably strong. The
premium for larger fish normalised towards the end of the quarter, and we have
strengthened our position in the strategically important US market. With global
supply expected to decline in Q4 and growth remaining limited in 2027, we see a
more favourable market balance ahead.
For 2026, we increase our smolt release in the Faroe Islands to 20.7 million
while maintaining our harvest guidance of 117,000 tonnes for the group. For
2027, we expect 97,000 tonnes in the Faroe Islands and 28,000 tonnes in
Scotland, totalling 125,000 tonnes. Our focus remains on strong biology,
improved cost efficiency and disciplined execution of our strategy to support
sustainable growth and long-term value creation."
During Q3 2026, the FOF segment sourced 9,587 tonnes (39,940 tonnes) of raw
material. The Operational EBIT margin was 24% (12%), and fish feed sales
amounted to 48,237 tonnes (49,087 tonnes).
For the first nine months of 2026, the FOF segment's operational EBIT margin was
21% (13%). During the first nine months of 2026, Havsbrún sourced 170,217 tonnes
(309,393 tonnes) of raw material.
In Q3 2026, the Freshwater segments in the Faroe Islands and Scotland
transferred a total of 7.4 million (8.4 million) smolts combined:
 - Freshwater FO: 4.5 million (4.8 million),
 - Freshwater SCT: 2.9 million (3.6 million).
For the first nine months of 2026, the freshwater segments have released a total
of 21.8 million (18.5 million) smolts:
 - Freshwater FO: 14.0 million (13.4 million),
 - Freshwater SCT: 7.8 million (5.1 million).
In Q3 2026, the Freshwater FO segment made an operational EBIT per kg
transferred smolt of DKK 32.34 (DKK 40.71), corresponding to NOK 47.31 (NOK
64.34). The Freshwater SCT segment made an operational EBIT per kg transferred
smolt of DKK -28.37 (DKK -66.88), corresponding to NOK -41.50 (NOK -105.70).
The Farming segments achieved higher prices in Q3 2026 than in Q3 2025. The
Farming segments had lower volumes in Q3 2026 compared to Q3 2025. In Q3 2026,
the Farming SCT segment had incident-based costs of DKK 42 million (DKK 70
million).
The total combined harvest in Q3 2026 of the farming segments in the Faroe
Islands and Scotland was 27,634 tonnes gutted weight (30,678 tgw):
 - Farming FO: 23,097 tgw (25,392 tgw),
 - Farming SCT: 4,537 tgw (5,286 tgw).
For the first nine months of 2026, the farming segments have harvested a total
of 88,865 tonnes gutted weight (78,932 tgw):
 - Farming FO: 74,985 tgw (60,326 tgw),
 - Farming SCT: 13,880 tgw (18,606 tgw).
In Q3 2026, the Farming FO segment made an operational EBIT per kg of DKK -0.34
(DKK -1.13), corresponding to NOK -0.50 (NOK -1.78). The Farming SCT segment
made an operational EBIT per kg of DKK -30.49 (DKK -36.09), corresponding to NOK
-44.60 (NOK -57.04).
The Services segment made an operational EBIT per kg of DKK 1.02 (DKK 1.25),
corresponding to NOK 1.49 (NOK 1.97). The operational EBIT margin for the
segment was 12% (15%).
The Sales & Other segment had a revenue of DKK 2,641 million (DKK 2,462 million)
and an operational EBIT margin of 2% (3%). The operational EBIT per kg was DKK
2.24 (DKK 2.37), corresponding to NOK 3.28 (NOK 3.75).

title: Odfjell Drilling Ltd. New Management Agreement and Contract Award for Beacon Pacific
body:
Odfjell Drilling Ltd is pleased to announce that Serica Energy (UK) Limited has entered into a drilling contract with Beacon Pacific Offshore Ltd for the sixth-generation semi-submersible rig, Beacon Pacific. 
The drilling programme covered by the drilling contract is scheduled to commence in the Q3 of 2027 and comprises a firm scope of six wells along with further options for additional activity in the region.
Odfjell Drilling will carry out the operational management of the Beacon Pacific throughout the duration of the contract with Serica Energy, including the mobilisation and transit of the rig to the United Kingdom. 
Reactivation activities have already partially begun ahead of Odfjell Drilling taking over management of the rig.
Kjetil Gjersdal, Chief Executive Officer of Odfjell Drilling AS commented: 
"We are delighted to support the owners of the Beacon Pacific and Serica Energy on this exciting project and look forward to expanding our fleet to nine high-spec harsh environment drilling rigs. The Beacon Pacific is similar in capability and specification to the Deepsea Yantai, which we have been managing for many years now. 
"This is an exciting new opportunity for us and we look forward to working collaboratively with all parties to prepare the rig for operations and execute a successful drilling campaign in the UK sector."

title: Endúr ASA - Contract award Engelsen Total
category: ADDITIONAL REGULATED INFORMATION REQUIRED TO BE DISCLOSED UNDER THE LAWS OF A MEMBER STATE
body:
2 November 2026 - Engelsen Total AS ("Engelsen Total"), a wholly owned subsidiary of Endúr ASA ("Endúr") platform company, Total Betong AS ("Totalbetong"), has been awarded a contract by Storebø Maritim AS ("Storebø Maritim"). The contract has a value of approximately NOK ~90 million excluding VAT.
Engelsen Total will act as turnkey supplier for the design and construction of Storebø Brygge in Austevoll. The project consists of an apartment building with an incorporated commercial unit. Design and engineering have started with on-site construction works expected to commence at the turn of the year 2026/2027, subject to Storebø Maritim's FID in November 2026. The project will have an estimated building period of 13 months.

title: TILBAKEKJØP AV EGNE EGENKAPITALBEVIS I SPAREBANK 1 HELGELAND
category: ACQUISITION OR DISPOSAL OF AN ISSUER'S OWN SHARES
body:
NOT FOR DISTRIBUTION OR RELEASE, DIRECTLY OR INDIRECTLY, IN OR INTO THE UNITED STATES OR ANY OTHER JURISDICTION IN WHICH THE DISTRIBUTION OR RELEASE WOULD BE UNLAWFUL. PLEASE SEE THE IMPORTANT NOTICE AT THE END OF THIS COMMUNICATION.
SpareBank 1 Helgeland ("Banken") har engasjert Norne Securities ("Tilretteleggeren") for å undersøke muligheten for et tilbakekjøp av inntil 30 000 egenkapitalbevis i Banken ("Tilbudet"). Egenkapitalbevisene skal brukes i forbindelse med Bankens gave til ansatte, og spareprogram for ansatte. Det vises for øvrig til protokoll fra Forstanderskapsmøte publisert av Banken 24. mars 2026 og tilbakekjøpsfullmakt registrert i Foretaksregisteret 10. oktober 2026.
Tilbudet vil bli gjennomført som en omvendt bookbuilding. Tilretteleggeren vil ta imot og akkumulere salgsordre fra eksisterende egenkapitalbeviseiere. En plassert salgsordre kan ikke trekkes tilbake eller endres av den selgende egenkapitalbeviseieren. Den selgende egenkapitalbeviseieren plikter å selge de tilbudte egenkapitalbevisene til Banken til de tilbudte vilkårene hvis og på det tidspunkt tilbudet er akseptert av Banken, uavhengig av om Banken beslutter å kjøpe et lavere antall egenkapitalbevis fra den selgende egenkapitalbeviseieren enn den respektive egenkapitalbeviseieren hadde tilbudt for salg. Den endelige kjøpsprisen per egenkapitalbevis vil bli fastsatt basert på salgsordre mottatt på et nivå som representerer en tilfredsstillende pris og et tilfredsstillende transaksjonsvolum (etter Bankens vurdering). Den endelige kjøpsprisen vil være identisk for alle selgende egenkapitalbeviseiere.
Akseptperioden starter omgående og er forventet avsluttet 3. november 2025 kl. 16:00. Banken og Tilretteleggeren forbeholder seg retten til å utvide akseptperioden.
Dersom transaksjonen gjennomføres, vil prissetting følge omgående. Basert på det overfor angitte tidspunktet for utgang av akseptperioden, forventes allokering utført innen 3. november 2025 kl. 18:00 (T), og oppgjør er forventet på eller rundt 5. november 2026 (T+2) gjennom en levering mot betaling (DVP) transaksjon. Hvis akseptperioden forlenges, vil disse datoene justeres tilsvarende.
Dersom totalt antall mottatte salgsordre på den endelige kjøpsprisen overgår 30 000 egenkapitalbevis (eller et lavere antall egenkapitalbevis Banken ønsker å kjøpe tilbake), vil allokering bli foretatt, i så stor utstrekning som mulig, på pro rata basis basert på det tilbudte volumet fra hver selgende egenkapitalbeviseier, med formål om å likebehandle alle egenkapitalbeviseiere basert på deres indikerte interesse i Tilbudet på den endelige kjøpsprisen. 
Egenkapitalbeviseiere som ønsker å delta i Tilbudet kan kontakte Norne Securities AS på +47 55 55 91 37 / +47 55 55 91 64 for å plassere salgsordre.
Tillatelse er gitt av Forstanderskapet i Banken og av Finanstilsynet.

title: DNB Bank ASA - status of share buy-back programme after week 44 2026
category: ACQUISITION OR DISPOSAL OF AN ISSUER'S OWN SHARES
body:
On 21 October 2026, DNB Bank ASA ("DNB") announced that the company has decided
to initiate a share buy-back programme comprising up to 0.75 per cent of the
company's own shares, which represents a total of 10,804,986 shares.
Up to 7,131,291 shares will be purchased on trading venues by 18 December 2026,
and a proposal to cancel the shares will be submitted to the next Annual General
Meeting. At the same meeting it will also be proposed to redeem the remaining
shares - up to 3,673,695 shares - from the Norwegian Government, represented by
the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Fisheries ("NFD"), so that NFD's ownership
interest of 34 per cent remains unchanged.
The total consideration paid for the shares purchased under the buy-back
programme, including the shares that will be proposed redeemed from NFD, will
not exceed NOK 3,790 million.
During week 44 of 2026, DNB purchased 940,500 own shares at an average price of
NOK 321.3362. Following this, DNB has purchased a total of 1,640,500 own shares
under the current buy-back programme, corresponding to 0.11% percent of the
shares in the company.

title: SpareBank 1 Ringerike Hadeland: Mulig tilbakekjøp av opptil 5.000 egne egenkapitalbevis
category: ADDITIONAL REGULATED INFORMATION REQUIRED TO BE DISCLOSED UNDER THE LAWS OF A MEMBER STATE
body:
SpareBank 1 Ringerike Hadeland har engasjert SB1 Markets AS for å undersøke muligheten for tilbakekjøp av opptil 5.000 egenkapitalbevis i banken til bruk i bankens spareprogram for ansatte. Egenkapitalbevisene skal viderefordeles til bankens ansatte i overensstemmelse med bankens spareprogram. Tilbakekjøpet vil bli gjennomført som en omvendt bookbuilding. Banken eier i dag 119 egne egenkapitalbevis.
Akseptperioden starter omgående med forventet avslutning 6. november 2026 kl. 16:00. Akseptperioden kan bli stengt på et tidligere tidspunkt. Banken og tilrettelegger forbeholder seg retten til å utvide akseptperioden og å akseptere ordre mottatt etter avslutning av akseptperioden.
Endelig kjøpspris per egenkapitalbevis vil bli fastsatt basert på mottatte salgsordre som, etter bankens vurdering, representerer en tilfredsstillende pris og transaksjonsvolum. Den endelige
kjøpsprisen vil være identisk for alle selgende egenkapitalbeviseiere. Banken forbeholder seg retten til å redusere antall egenkapitalbevis som kjøpes, alternativt til ikke å kjøpe noen egenkapitalbevis.
Dersom totalt antall mottatte salgsordre på den endelige kjøpsprisen overstiger det antall egenkapitalbevis som banken beslutter å erverve, vil avkorting bli foretatt. Allokering vil i så stor utstrekning som mulig bli gjort på pro rata basis basert på det tilbudte volumet fra hver selgende egenkapitalbeviseier. Formålet er å likebehandle alle egenkapitalbeviseiere basert på deres indikerte interesse i tilbudet på den endelige kjøpsprisen. 
Mottatte salgsordre er bindende og ugjenkallelige og kan ikke trekkes tilbake, kanselleres eller endres av den selgende egenkapitalbeviseieren etter at den har blitt mottatt av tilrettelegger. Den selgende egenkapitalbeviseieren plikter å selge de tilbudte egenkapitalbevisene til banken til de tilbudte vilkårene hvis og på det tidspunkt tilbudet er akseptert av banken, uavhengig av om banken beslutter å kjøpe et lavere antall egenkapitalbevis fra den selgende egenkapitalbeviseieren enn den respektive egenkapitalbeviseieren hadde tilbudt for salg.
Dersom transaksjonen gjennomføres, vil prissetting følge omgående etter utløp av akseptperioden. Basert på det ovenfor angitte tidspunktet for avslutning av akseptperioden, forventes allokering utført 6. november 2026 (T), og oppgjør er forventet på eller rundt 10. november 2026 (T+2) gjennom en levering mot betaling (DVP)-transaksjon. Hvis akseptperioden forlenges, vil disse datoene justeres tilsvarende. 
Tilbakekjøpet er basert på fullmakt fra bankens ordinære representantskapsmøte den 26. mars 2026.
Egenkapitalbeviseiere som har spørsmål om transaksjonen og ønsker å selge egenkapitalbevis, bes kontakte Joakim Hafsmo i SB1 Markets AS på:

title: Rehabilitation Contract Awarded by Norwegian Property at Fornebu
body:
Betonmast, a subsidiary of AF Gruppen, has entered into an agreement for the rehabilitation of Snarøyveien 30, Buildings J and K, at Fornebu. The contract is a design and build contract valued at approximately NOK 400 million, excluding VAT.
The project comprises the rehabilitation of approximately 34,000 square metres of office space in the former Telenor headquarters at Fornebu, including upgrades to technical systems and tenant adaptations. Parts of the buildings will remain operational throughout the construction period. 
"We are pleased to embark on a new collaboration with Norwegian Property. The buildings at Snarøyveien 30 play a key role in the continued development of Fornebu, and it is inspiring to contribute to the modernization of these office facilities," says Peter Sandrup, CEO of Betonmast.

title: The Swedish Competition Authority approves Telenor Sverige's acquisition of a controlling stake in Bahnhof
body:
The Swedish Competition Authority has today approved Telenor Sverige's acquisition of a controlling stake in Bahnhof AB (publ). Telenor Sverige also obtained the required foreign direct investment clearance from the Inspectorate of Strategic Products (ISP) on 20 October 2026. Accordingly, all regulatory conditions for completion of Telenor Sverige's acquisitions of shares in Bahnhof from Jon Karlung and Andreas Norman, directly and indirectly through K.N. Telecom AB, and Investment AB Öresund (the "Acquisitions"), have now been satisfied.
Next steps
Telenor will now complete the remaining steps towards completion of the Acquisitions, which comprise 57.5% of the shares and 87.9% of the votes in Bahnhof and is expected shortly.
Following completion, Telenor Sverige will become the controlling shareholder in Bahnhof and will be required to make a mandatory cash offer to the remaining shareholders of Bahnhof. As previously communicated, Telenor Sverige intends to launch the mandatory cash offer at SEK 62 per share as soon as practicable following completion.
For further transaction details, please refer to Telenor's stock exchange announcement of 8 July 2026.

title: OKEA ASA - Third quarter 2026 financial results
body:
(Trondheim, 3 November 2026) - In the third quarter of 2026, OKEA ASA (OSE:
OKEA) increased the cash balance to USD 476 (355) million, resulting in a net
cash position of USD 180 (59) million. The company delivered strong operational
performance with operating income totaling USD 332 (334) million and EBITDA
totalling USD 192 (207) million. Net profit amounted to USD 29 (14) million.
Bestla is expected on stream before year-end, ahead of schedule and at a lower
expected cost than previous estimates. The strengthened financial position and
outlook support the resumption of quarterly dividends, with the first dividend
payment of NOK 2.00 per share already in December 2026. The company also intends
to maintain quarterly distributions of at least NOK 1.00 per share throughout
2027.
(Amounts in parentheses refer to previous quarter)
"I am very pleased with the strong operational execution during the third
quarter. With Garn West South now on stream and the planned maintenance campaign
at Draugen successfully completed, we are well positioned to deliver 2026
production towards the high end of our guidance range.
With Bestla also nearing completion and Springmus East sanctioned, OKEA is
closer to an important inflection point, with investments made over recent years
translating into higher production, while investment levels are declining and
becoming increasingly focused on flexible, shorter-cycle opportunities. This
increases our financial flexibility, and I am particularly pleased to announce
that we will resume quarterly dividends, with the first dividend payment in
December 2026," stated OKEA CEO Svein J. Liknes.
Third quarter 2026 summary
Net production was 29.1 (27.0) kboepd and production efficiency was 89% (83%).
The increase mainly reflects fewer planned maintenance shutdowns compared with
the previous quarter. Maintenance in the third quarter was primarily related to
Draugen, compared with Brage, Statfjord B and Ivar Aasen in the second quarter.
Revenues from sales of petroleum products amounted to USD 316 (313) million
based on sold volumes of 33.4 (34.4) kboepd. Higher realised natural gas prices
of USD 121.3 (88.1) per boe more than offset lower sold volumes and lower
realised crude prices. Realised liquids prices were USD 96.6 (116.9) per boe for
crude and USD 58.4 (55.3) per boe for NGL. With NGLs constituting 5% (21%) of
liquids volumes sold, the average realised liquids price ended at USD 94.6
(104.2) per boe.
Total operating income amounted to USD 332 (334) million, including other
operating income of USD 16 (21) million. Other operating income comprises a gain
of USD 28 (0) million from the sale of the Mistral licence and tariff income at
Gjøa and Statfjord of USD 7 (6) million, partly offset by a net hedging loss of
USD 20 (gain of 15) million, mainly related to oil hedges.
Production expenses amounted to USD 87 (89) million, corresponding to USD 29.5
(34.0) per boe. The lower unit cost was mainly driven by higher production and
lower maintenance costs, with the planned maintenance campaign primarily related
to Draugen in the quarter.
Changes in over-/underlift positions and production inventory resulted in an
expense of USD 20 (28) million, as sold volumes exceeded produced volumes.
Depreciation of oil and gas properties amounted to USD 56 (47) million. The
increase was mainly due to higher production.
Impairments amounted to USD 33 (94) million. The impairment related to Statfjord
and was driven by reduced volume estimates and increased capex, partly offset by
higher forward prices. The related post-tax expense was USD 7 (27) million.
Exploration and evaluation expenses amounted to USD 28 (5) million. The increase
was mainly due to the expensing of USD 23 million of previously capitalised
costs related to Alpehumle and Prince.
Tax expense amounted to USD 77 (51) million and net profit after tax ended at
USD 29 (14) million.
Strong operational performance resulted in cash flow from operations of USD 182
(179) million. Net cash outflow from investment activities was USD 67 (77)
million, including receipt of proceeds from the sale of the Mistral licence.
Investments in oil and gas properties amounted to USD 81 (74) million, mainly
related to production drilling at Draugen and Statfjord and progress on the
Bestla and Power from Shore development projects.
The cash balance ended at USD 414 (296) million. In addition, USD 62 (59)
million was invested in money market funds classified as other assets. With
interest-bearing bond loans of USD 296 (296) million, the net cash position
increased to USD 180 (59) million.
Guidance
Following strong operational execution in the third quarter and the start-up of
Garn West South, production guidance for 2026 is narrowed to 31-32 kboepd from
29-32 kboepd. Production guidance for 2027 remains unchanged at 39-43 kboepd.
Capex guidance for 2026 is narrowed to USD 320-340 million from USD 300-360
million. For 2027, capex guidance is increased to USD 260-320 million from USD
230-290 million, reflecting the accelerated drilling of the Springmus East
production well at Draugen.
Webcast and audio conference
A presentation of the results with a Q&A session will be held today through a
webcast and audio conference starting 10:00 CET. The presentation will be held
by Svein J. Liknes (CEO) and Birte Norheim (CFO).

title: SalMar - Rekordhøyt slaktevolum og betydelig resultatforbedring
body:
Rekordhøyt slaktevolum og fortsatt gode operasjonelle og biologiske prestasjoner
bidro til betydelig resultatforbedring sammenlignet med samme periode i fjor.
Høyere volum, lavere kostnadsnivå og bedre prisoppnåelse bidro positivt,
samtidig som Salg & Industri leverte et sterkt resultat. Sterk kontantstrøm fra
driften bidro også til ytterligere reduksjon i netto rentebærende gjeld og en
styrket finansiell posisjon.
Operasjonell EBIT for konsernet var 1 609 millioner kroner i tredje kvartal
2026. Slaktevolumet var rekordhøye 105 100 tonn og operasjonell EBIT per kg var
15,3 kroner. For Norge var operasjonell EBIT 1 620 millioner kroner,
slaktevolumet var 99 900 tonn og operasjonell EBIT per kg var 16,2 kroner.
 * Rekordhøyt slaktevolum, drevet av de gode biologiske prestasjonene gjennom
 2026.
 * Sterkt resultat fra Salg & Industri, drevet av rekordhøye volum gjennom
 anleggene, forbedrede operasjonelle prestasjoner og solide salgsresultater.
 * Icelandic Salmon tilbake med positivt resultat, drevet av lavere
 kostnadsnivå og god prisoppnåelse.
 * Betydelig høyere slaktevolum fra Scottish Sea Farms, men resultatet var
 fortsatt svakt som følge av biologiske utfordringer.
- Rekordhøyt slaktevolum og betydelig resultatforbedring viser effekten av den
gode biologiske utviklingen gjennom 2026. Den underliggende biologiske statusen
er god, og sammen med lavere kost på fisken vi har i sjøen gir dette et godt
utgangspunkt for fortsettelsen, sier Frode Arntsen, konsernsjef i SalMar ASA.
Styrket finansiell posisjon
SalMar styrket sin finansielle posisjon ytterligere i tredje kvartal. Netto
rentebærende gjeld ble redusert med 1 228 millioner kroner fra utgangen av andre
kvartal til 17 912 millioner kroner. Sammenlignet med samme periode i fjor er
netto rentebærende gjeld redusert med 3 739 millioner kroner. NIBD/EBITDA ble
redusert til 2,1, fra 2,5 ved utgangen av andre kvartal og 4,0 ved utgangen av
tredje kvartal 2025.
Samtidig økte egenkapitalandelen til 36,0 prosent, og SalMar hadde ved utgangen
av kvartalet 15,9 milliarder kroner i tilgjengelig likviditet. Dette gir
selskapet et solid finansielt handlingsrom, herunder for gjennomføring av
Måsøval-transaksjonen når nødvendige regulatoriske godkjennelser foreligger.
Forventer noe lavere kostnadsnivå og guider et slaktevolum på 348 000 tonn i
2027
For fjerde kvartal 2026 forventer SalMar et noe lavere kostnadsnivå i
verdikjeden sammenlignet med tredje kvartal. Samtidig forventes lavere
slaktevolum i Norge sammenlignet med fjerde kvartal 2025.
Volumguidingen for 2026 er 347 000 tonn, inkludert relativ andel fra Scottish
Sea Farms. Dette tilsvarer en vekst i slaktevolum på 15 prosent sammenlignet med
2025. Guidingen for Norge er uendret, mens volumforventningene for Icelandic
Salmon og Scottish Sea Farms er noe redusert.
For 2027 forventer SalMar et samlet slaktevolum på 348 000 tonn, inkludert
relativ andel fra Scottish Sea Farms, på samme nivå som i 2026. Dette inkluderer
307 000 tonn fra Norge og SalMar Ocean, 18 000 tonn fra Icelandic Salmon og
45 000 tonn fra Scottish Sea Farms på 100-prosentbasis. Måsøval er ikke
inkludert i volumguidingen for 2027 ettersom transaksjonen fortsatt er betinget
av relevante regulatoriske godkjennelser.
SalMar forventer lav global tilbudsvekst i 2027 og opplever fortsatt sterk
etterspørsel etter sine produkter.
Prosessen for Måsøval-transaksjonen går som planlagt
I juli 2026 inngikk SalMar ASA avtale med Heimstø AS om å kjøpe Heimstøs
85 727 553 aksjer i Måsøval AS, tilsvarende om lag 70 prosent av aksjekapitalen.
Kjøpesummen er 39,50 kroner per aksje, tilsvarende et samlet vederlag på om lag
3,4 milliarder kroner. Transaksjonen er betinget av vanlige
gjennomføringsvilkår, inkludert relevante regulatoriske godkjennelser. Prosessen
med å innhente nødvendige regulatoriske godkjennelser går som planlagt.
Transaksjonen forventes å gi SalMar en enda sterkere plattform for videre
bærekraftig vekst i Midt-Norge, med potensial for bedre utnyttelse av ressurser,
kompetanse og infrastruktur, samt videre utvikling på laksens betingelser og
langsiktig verdiskaping langs norskekysten.
Full rapport og presentasjon for tredje kvartal er vedlagt.
SalMars konsernsjef Frode Arntsen og CFO Ulrik Steinvik vil presentere
selskapets resultater i dag kl. 08:00 på Hotel Continental i Oslo.

title: SalMar - Record-high harvest volume and significant improvement in results
body:
Record-high harvest volume and continued strong operational and biological
performance contributed to a significant improvement in results compared with
the same period last year. Higher volumes, lower cost levels and improved price
achievement contributed positively, while Sales & Industry delivered strong
results. Strong cash flow from operations also contributed to a further
reduction in net interest-bearing debt and a strengthened financial position.
Operational EBIT for the Group was NOK 1,609 million in the third quarter of
2026. Harvest volume reached a record-high 105,100 tonnes, and Operational EBIT
per kg was NOK 15.3. In Norway, Operational EBIT was NOK 1,620 million, harvest
volume was 99,900 tonnes and Operational EBIT per kg was NOK 16.2.
 * Record-high harvest volume, driven by strong biological performance
 throughout 2026.
 * Strong results from Sales & Industry, driven by record-high volumes through
 the processing facilities, improved operational performance and solid sales
 results.
 * Icelandic Salmon returned to positive results, driven by a lower cost level
 and good price achievement.
 * Significantly higher harvest volume from Scottish Sea Farms, although
 results remained weak due to biological challenges.
"Record-high harvest volume and a significant improvement in results reflect the
strong biological development throughout 2026. The underlying biological status
remains good, and together with lower costs for the fish currently in the sea,
this provides a solid foundation going forward," says Frode Arntsen, CEO of
SalMar ASA.
Strengthened financial position
SalMar further strengthened its financial position in the third quarter. Net
interest-bearing debt was reduced by NOK 1,228 million from the end of the
second quarter to NOK 17,912 million. Compared with the same period last year,
net interest-bearing debt has been reduced by NOK 3,739 million. NIBD/EBITDA was
reduced to 2.1, from 2.5 at the end of the second quarter and 4.0 at the end of
the third quarter of 2025.
At the same time, the equity ratio increased to 36.0 per cent, and SalMar had
NOK 15.9 billion in available liquidity at the end of the quarter. This provides
the company with solid financial flexibility, including for the completion of
the Måsøval transaction once the necessary regulatory approvals have been
obtained.
Expecting slightly lower cost level and guiding harvest volume of 346,000 tonnes
for 2027
For the fourth quarter of 2026, SalMar expects a slightly lower cost level in
the value chain compared with the third quarter. At the same time, lower harvest
volume in Norway is expected compared with the fourth quarter of 2025.
Harvest volume guidance for 2026 is 347,000 tonnes, including the relative share
from Scottish Sea Farms. This represents harvest volume growth of 15 per cent
compared with 2025. Guidance for Norway remains unchanged, while volume
expectations for Icelandic Salmon and Scottish Sea Farms have been somewhat
reduced.
For 2027, SalMar expects total harvest volume of 348,000 tonnes, including the
relative share from Scottish Sea Farms, in line with 2026. This includes
307,000 tonnes from Norway and SalMar Ocean, 18,000 tonnes from Icelandic Salmon
and 45,000 tonnes from Scottish Sea Farms on a 100 per cent basis. Måsøval is
not included in the harvest volume guidance for 2027, as the transaction remains
subject to relevant regulatory approvals.
SalMar expects low global supply growth in 2027 and continues to see strong
demand for its products.
Måsøval transaction process progressing according to plan
In July 2026, SalMar ASA entered into an agreement with Heimstø AS to acquire
Heimstø's 85,727,553 shares in Måsøval AS, representing approximately 70 per
cent of the share capital. The purchase price is NOK 39.50 per share,
corresponding to a total consideration of approximately NOK 3.4 billion. The
transaction is subject to customary closing conditions, including relevant
regulatory approvals. The process of obtaining the necessary regulatory
approvals is progressing according to plan.
The transaction is expected to provide SalMar with an even stronger platform for
further sustainable growth in Central Norway, with potential for improved
utilisation of resources, expertise and infrastructure, as well as further
development on the salmon's terms and long-term value creation along the
Norwegian coast.

Norconsult: Q3 2026 - Continued growth and improved profitability
body:
Sandvika, 3 November 2026 (OSE: NORCO): The income after external project costs
increased by 6 percent to NOK 2 314 million (2 191) in the third quarter of
2026. Organic growth adjusted for calendar effects was 1 percent. The adjusted
EBITA margin adjusted for calendar effects was 9.8 percent in the quarter, up
from 9.3 percent in the corresponding quarter last year.
Highlights Q3 2026
 - Growth of 6 percent in income after external project cost to NOK 2 314
million (2 191)
 - Positive calendar effects of NOK 17 million
 - Organic growth of 1 percent adjusted for calendar effects
 - Adj. EBITA was NOK 242 million (204) with an adj. EBITA margin of 10.4
percent (9.3)
 - Adj. EBITA margin was 9.8 percent, adjusted for calendar effects
 - Net profit of NOK 118 million (132)
 - Earnings per share (EPS) NOK 0.38 (0.43)
 - Order backlog increased to NOK 7.9 billion, up from NOK 7.8 billion in Q2
2026
Comments from CEO Egil Hogna:
"Norconsult delivered continued growth and improved profitability in the third
quarter, in a market environment that remained broadly stable across the
Nordics. During the quarter Norconsult has taken significant steps in the use of
AI in our architecture, engineering and business activities across the
organization."
Outlook:
The overall market is expected to remain stable, however, with continued
uncertainty linked to the geopolitical situation.
The demand in Infrastructure is expected to be stable going forward in line with
public spending plans. The private market for Buildings & Architecture is
expected to continue as-is. We continue to expect a high level of activity in
the energy sector, and a more mixed development in other industry segments as
geopolitical factors may further delay investment decisions in certain markets.
Norconsult has considerable flexibility with a diversified mix of services and
end-market exposures in the Nordics. Most of the demand for our services comes
from the public sector. This makes Norconsult less exposed towards short-term
cyclicality in the economy in general.
Norconsult will continue to take proactive measures to improve underlying
profitability and maintain efficiency in selected parts of the business.

title: Odfjell Drilling Ltd. Reports for the Third Quarter of 2026
body:
Kjetil Gjersdal, Chief Executive Officer of Odfjell Drilling AS commented:
"During Q3, we overcame one of our toughest operational challenges in recent years while at the same time, securing industry-leading contract rates for our units. As a result, Odfjell Drilling is now back to full strength and, in the last few months, we have been awarded contracts which are cumulatively worth well over USD 700 million.
"Our new contract with Vår Energi for the Deepsea Bergen extends the rig's firm backlog to early 2031, with priced options running to 2035. This contract provides long-term visibility and underlines both the demand for our units and the strength of a market we expect to continue to tighten.
"While our reported results still reflect periods of downtime, I am proud of how our teams responded and of the resilience the business has shown. We enter Q4 with our entire owned fleet in operation, a larger backlog and a clear path to generating more value for our shareholders."
Q3 Highlights:
GOOD FINANCIAL RESULTS BUT IMPACTED BY DOWNTIME
- EBITDA of USD 130 million from Operating Revenue of USD 265 million

BALANCE SHEET REMAINS ROBUST

DIVIDEND INCREASED

title: Sterk vekst og styrket rentenetto i tredje kvartal
body:
SpareBank 1 Østfold Akershus leverte et resultat før skatt på 197 mill. kroner i tredje kvartal 2026 (195 mill. kroner i fjor). Resultatet etter skatt var 156 mill. kroner (157 mill. kroner), egenkapitalavkastningen 11,9 prosent (12,2 prosent) og resultat fra ordinær drift 179 mill. kroner (177 mill. kroner). Kvartalet var preget av sterk utlånsvekst, god kredittkvalitet og et godt resultatbidrag fra SpareBank 1 Gruppen. Rentenetto inklusive provisjoner fra kredittforetak økte til 1,76 prosent fra 1,64 prosent i forrige kvartal.
Hittil i år var resultatet før skatt 565 mill. kroner (620 mill. kroner), resultatet etter skatt 466 mill. kroner (514 mill. kroner) og egenkapitalavkastningen 12,2 prosent (13,9 prosent). Resultat fra ordinær drift var 441 mill. kroner (466 mill. kroner). Inntektene er på nivå med fjoråret, mens høyere kostnader og tap samt lavere nettoinntekter fra finansielle instrumenter trekker resultatet ned. Tapsprosenten har økt til 0,11 prosent (0,07 prosent), men er fortsatt lav. Banken har samtidig styrket markedsposisjonen, med en utlånsvekst på 9,2 prosent de siste 12 månedene.
Vi leverer et godt tredje kvartal med sterk vekst og en tydelig bedring i rentenettoen. Samtidig fortsetter vi å ta markedsandeler i både privat- og bedriftsmarkedet. Vi har gjennom året tatt grep for å styrke kostnadseffektiviteten, og går inn i de kommende kvartalene med god kredittkvalitet og en solid finansiell posisjon. Dette gir oss et godt utgangspunkt for videre lønnsom vekst, sier administrerende direktør Arild Bjørn Hansen.
Styrker posisjonen og tar markedsandeler
Bankens samlede utlån inklusive overførte lån til kredittforetak var 44,2 mrd. kroner ved utgangen av tredje kvartal, tilsvarende en vekst på 9,2 prosent de siste 12 månedene. Tolvmånedersveksten var 7,5 prosent i privatmarkedet og 14,4 prosent i bedriftsmarkedet.
I privatmarkedet har banken fortsatt å styrke markedsposisjonen i regionen. I bedriftsmarkedet kommer veksten både fra eksisterende og nye kunder og vurderes å være innenfor bankens risikovilje og strategiske ambisjoner. Veksten viser at vi lykkes med vår langsiktige strategi og styrker posisjonen i markedsområdet. Fremover vil vi videreføre strategien med selektiv vekst, sterk risikostyring og tett kundeoppfølging. Lokalkunnskap, nærhet til kundene og gode rådgivere er viktige konkurransefortrinn for oss, sier Arild Bjørn Hansen.
God kredittkvalitet og lave tap
Tap på utlån og garantier var 11 mill. kroner i tredje kvartal, mot 13 mill. kroner i samme periode i fjor. Tapsprosenten hittil i år er 0,11 prosent. Kredittkvaliteten er fortsatt god, uten vesentlige negative utslag av endrede markedsforhold. Banken følger eiendom tett, og utviklingen i mislighold, tapsavsetninger og risikoklassifisering er stabil.
Kostnadstiltak skal styrke lønnsomheten
Kostnadsprogrammet som ble iverksatt tidligere i år er gjennomført som planlagt. Bemanningen i morbanken reduseres med 20 årsverk på frivillig basis innen utgangen av 2026, og banken har i tillegg identifisert og iverksatt kostnadsreduksjoner med en forventet årlig effekt på 10 mill. kroner.
Kostnadsprosenten falt fra 41,8 prosent i andre kvartal, til 39,9 prosent i tredje kvartal. Hittil i år er kostnadsprosenten 43,3 prosent, eller 41,8 prosent korrigert for kostnadene knyttet til bemanningsreduksjonen. Vi har tatt konkrete grep for å styrke kostnadseffektiviteten. Effekten kommer gradvis, og tiltakene vil få full effekt i 2027. Ambisjonen er å kombinere fortsatt vekst med bedre effektivitet og dermed styrke lønnsomheten over tid, sier Arild Bjørn Hansen.
Godt posisjonert for videre lønnsom vekst
Utsikter til høyere renter over lengre tid demper forventet press på netto renteinntekter, men sterk konkurranse og press på utlånsmarginene kan påvirke inntektene fremover. Etter Norges Banks renteheving på 0,25 prosentpoeng 24. september 2026 besluttet banken å øke boliglåns- og innskuddsrentene med inntil 0,25 prosentpoeng, med full effekt fra 28. november 2026.
Konsernet har god ren kjernekapitaldekning forholdsmessig konsolidert på 17,08 prosent ved utgangen av tredje kvartal, over styrets minimumsmål på 16,07 prosent. Sterk markedsposisjon, god kredittkvalitet, bedret rentenetto, kostnadstiltak og fortsatt vekst gir et godt grunnlag for økt lønnsomhet. Vi viderefører strategien med god risikostyring og lønnsom vekst, avslutter Arild Bjørn Hansen.

Multiconsult third quarter 2026 results
body:
Multiconsult's performance gradually improved towards the end of the quarter,
reflecting early effects of measures to strengthen operational efficiency. Order
intake was solid, while the billing ratio in September exceeded the level
recorded in September last year.
"Although the third quarter results were not at the level of our long-term
ambitions, we saw positive developments towards the end of the period. Order
intake and cost control were solid and measures we have implemented to improve
profitability are starting to take effect," says interim CEO Kristin Olsson
Augestad.
In the quarter, net operating revenues increased by 2.0 per cent to NOK 1 219.7
million, while organic revenue growth adjusted for calendar effects and
acquisitions was 0.1 per cent. Order intake was solid at NOK 1 355 million, an
increase of 12.4 per cent compared with the same quarter last year.
Profitability was impacted by a low activity level in the summer months and
transaction costs related to the proposed merger with Rejlers, while
profitability improved in September as measures to strengthen operational
efficiency started to take effect. EBITA amounted to NOK 6.3 million (62.1),
corresponding to a margin of 0.5 per cent (5.2). EBITA adjusted amounted to NOK
45.0 million (67.2), corresponding to a margin of 3.7 per cent (5.6). The
billing ratio remained unchanged at 70.1 per cent (70.1), while higher billing
rates contributed positively.
Third quarter 2026
 - A major strategic step is the merger plan with Rejlers
 - Operational efficiency contributed to improved profitability in September,
however challenging summer months resulted in weaker profitability for the
quarter
 - Net operating revenues increased by 2.0 per cent to NOK 1 219.7 million (1
196.4)
 - The organic revenue growth adjusted for the calendar effect was 0.1 per
cent
 - EBITA of NOK 6.3 million (62.1), equal to an EBITA margin of 0.5 per cent
(5.2)
 - EBITA adjusted was NOK 45.0 million (67.2), equal to an EBITA margin of 3.7
per cent (5.6)
 - EBITA was negatively impacted by NOK 38.3 million in transaction and
restructuring costs related to the merger and internal resources (write-downs)
and legal expenses related to the Sotra Link project of NOK 0.4 million
 - Restructuring costs of NOK 8.4 million related to measures to improve
profitability, not adjusted for in EBITA adjusted
 - Billing ratio of 70.1 per cent (70.1)
 - Strong order intake of NOK 1 355 million (1 205)
 - Strong order backlog of NOK 3 823 million (4 316), complemented by a
significant volume of framework agreements
 - Full-time equivalents (FTE) decreased by 0.3 per cent, to 3 731 (3 744)
 - Net profit of NOK -20.9 million (38.9)
 - Earnings per share of NOK -0.74 (1.41)
 - The overall market outlook remains stable
Year to date 2026
 - Net operating revenues of NOK 4 354.7 million (4 135.7), a y-o-y growth of
5.3 per cent
 - The organic revenue growth adjusted for the calendar effect was 1.9 per
cent
 - EBITA of NOK 275.1 million (319.9), equal to an EBITA margin of 6.3 per cent
(7.7)
 - Net operating revenues and EBITA were impacted by a positive calendar
effect of NOK 7.0 million compared with 2025
 - EBITA adjusted was NOK 299.3 million (338.8), equal to an EBITA margin of
6.9 per cent (8.2)
 - EBITA was negatively impacted by net costs of NOK 24.2 million related to
transaction and restructuring costs related to merger and a positive reversal
from the Sotra Link project
 - Restructuring costs of NOK 17.7 million related to measures to improve
profitability, not adjusted for in EBITA adjusted
 - Billing ratio of 71.2 per cent (71.8), down 0.5 pp
 - Strong order intake of NOK 4 802 million (4 441)
 - Net profit of NOK 178.1 million (213.9)
 - Earnings per share of NOK 6.48 (7.75)
 - Full-time equivalents (FTE) increased by 2.9 per cent, to 3 812 (3 703)
Merger supports growth ambitions
On 7 September, Multiconsult and Rejlers announced the plan to create a leading
Nordic multidisciplinary consultancy group. The merger planwas approved by the
general meetings in both companies on 19 October.
"Together, we will create a leading engineering, architecture and consultancy
group with nearly 8 000 employees across the Nordics. Our ambition is to be a
natural choice for large and complex projects. We also aim to take a leading
position in energy, industry and defence-related assignments," says Kristin
Olsson Augestad.
The companies expect the merger to be completed around year-end 2026 or at the
beginning of 2027, subject to the necessary regulatory approvals and fulfilment
or waiver of the other conditions set out in the merger plan.
"As we begin the important work ahead of the merger, we remain fully focused on
operations and sales. It is business as usual across Multiconsult," says Kristin
Olsson Augestad.

title: LINK Mobility - Q3 2026 - Back to high-single-digit organic growth
category: ADDITIONAL REGULATED INFORMATION REQUIRED TO BE DISCLOSED UNDER THE LAWS OF A MEMBER STATE
body:
(Oslo, 4 November 2026) - LINK Mobility delivered organic gross profit growth of 7% in Q3 2026, at the high end of expectations and marking a clear acceleration from the second quarter. Gross profit adjusted for organic currency movements was NOK 508 million, reflecting a negative currency impact of NOK 25 million in the quarter. With the current momentum expected to continue into Q4, LINK raises its H2 2026 organic gross profit growth guidance to high single digits. The current strong commercial momentum and improving growth indicators support our expectation of high-single-digit organic gross profit growth in 2027, in line with our medium-term ambition. Alongside the improved growth outlook, LINK expects shareholder distributions of NOK 330-400 million for fiscal year 2026.
Q3'26 confirms accelerating organic growth 
- Organic gross profit growth accelerated to 7% in Q3 2026, improving 5 percentage points quarter-on-quarter and reaching the high end of expectations.
- Organic gross profit growth improved, driven by Enterprise gross profit growth accelerating 4 ppts to 7%, while Global Messaging returned to positive growth.
- LINK raises its H2'26 organic gross profit growth guidance to high single digits, with continued momentum expected into Q4.
- Current trends support our expectation of high-single-digit organic gross profit growth in 2027.
- LINK expects shareholder distributions of NOK 330-400 million for FY2026, up 10-30% from FY2025, with share buybacks preferred at the current valuation.
"Organic growth remains a key priority for LINK, and our strong focus and execution throughout the quarter translated into clear improvements in our growth performance. This progress provides a strong foundation for continued organic growth into 2027, in line with our medium-term ambition. Looking further ahead, we expect increasing AI adoption to provide an additional structural tailwind, driving higher messaging volumes and greater adoption of richer conversational channels. Our strong balance sheet and cash generation allow us to increase shareholder distributions while continuing to invest in organic growth and value-accretive M&A," says Thomas Berge, CEO of LINK Mobility.

title: Bouvet ASA - Growth in number of employees, increased AI deployment and new contracts
body:
Bouvet reported operating revenues of NOK 865.4 million for the third quarter
of 2026, compared with NOK 870.5 million in the same period of last year.
Operating profit (EBIT) for the period amounted to NOK 80.5 million, compared
with NOK 91.6 million in the same period of 2025. 
For the first nine months Bouvet reported operating revenues of NOK 2 877.4
million, compared with NOK 2 913.9 million in the same period last year. For
the same period, the operating profit ended at NOK 329.8 million, compared
with NOK 370.1 million in the same period of 2025. 
"Our industry is developing and changing rapidly, and new technologies are
presenting new opportunities and making our service delivery more efficient.
Development and recruitment are needed to secure new and relevant expertise
for the group, and we are constantly working to tailor both our service
offering and our delivery models to market and client needs. This places
significant demands on us as a business. We have to be proactive to build
leading positions, and it is crucial that we streamline and improve our own
operations at the same time," says Per Gunnar Tronsli, CEO of Bouvet ASA.
Bouvet's total operating costs came to NOK 784.9 million for the third
quarter, compared with NOK 778.9 million in the same period of 2025. The EBIT
margin for the third quarter was 9.3 per cent, compared with 10.5 per cent in
the third quarter of 2025. Net profit came to NOK 59.5 million, compared with
NOK 70.1 million for the third quarter of 2025. Diluted earnings per share
were NOK 0.58 for the quarter, compared with NOK 0.68 in the same period of
last year. 
At a board meeting on 3 November 2026, the board of directors of Bouvet ASA
resolved to exercise the authorisation granted by the general meeting to
approve a supplementary dividend of NOK 0.70 per share in respect of the 2025
financial year. The share will be traded ex-dividend as of 6 November 2026,
and the dividend will be paid on 20 November 2026.

title: Panoro Energy - Trading Statement and Operations Update
body:
Oslo, 4 November 2026 - Panoro Energy ASA ("Panoro" or the "Company") provides
an update in advance of its Q3 2026 results which are scheduled for release on
18 November 2026. Information contained within this release is unaudited and may
be subject to further review and amendment.
Julien Balkany, Executive Chairman of Panoro, commented:
"The tragic incident involving the Prospector 5 rig at the Dussafu block on 24
October puts everything we report today into perspective. Our thoughts are first
and above all with those who have lost loved ones and with everyone affected. On
behalf of everyone at Panoro, I extend our deepest condolences to the bereaved
families and our heartfelt sympathy to the crew, their families, friends and
colleagues. We express our sincere gratitude and our full solidarity to the rig
owner, Borr Drilling, the operator, BW Energy, the Gabonese authorities and all
the emergency responders in their relentless efforts in the search and rescue
operations. The human consequences of this tragedy shall remain foremost in our
minds.
It is with this sense of profound sorrow that we fulfil our responsibility to
update our shareholders and other key stakeholders on the business. This has
been a transformational year for Panoro, marked by strong operational
performance and two major transactions that have broadened our production base
and strengthened the company. In September, we completed the second of these
substantial acquisitions, adding a high-quality gas producing asset in Côte
d'Ivoire and taking a significant step forward in the scale and diversification
of our business, specifically in light of the recent tragic incident.
Dussafu accounted for around 17 per cent of pro forma group production over the
first nine months of the year. The broader portfolio built through this year's
consecutive acquisitions provides greater resilience and strengthens our ability
to manage operational disruption.
We have also started the fourth quarter with strong price realisations on our
October oil sales achieving an average realised price of USD 127.5 per barrel to
date, a record high in Panoro's history.
As we look ahead, we do so mindful of the people affected by the Prospector 5
rig tragedy. Panoro enters this next chapter as a stronger, more diversified
company, well positioned to deliver sustainable and meaningful returns for
shareholders, while keeping the safety and wellbeing of those working across our
operations at the heart of our responsibilities."
Rig Incident at Dussafu
 - On 24 October 2026, the Prospector 5 jack-up drilling rig, owned and
operated by Borr Drilling, sank during preparations for the MaBoMo Phase 2
drilling campaign. The Company is assessing the impact of this tragic incident
on its future outlook

title: Cloudberry Clean Energy ASA | Third quarter 2026 report
body:
Oslo, Norway, 04 November 2026: Cloudberry Clean Energy ASA ("Cloudberry" or the
"Company") delivered record-high quarterly production and power-related
revenues, and nearly five times proportionate EBITDA growth compared to the same
quarter last year.
Financial highlights
 - Strong financial performance: Delivered strong financial growth, with
revenue more than doubling and EBITDA increasing almost 5x year-over-year on a
proportionate basis. Record-high production and higher realized power prices
compared to the same quarter last year resulted in Cloudberry's highest
quarterly power-related revenues to date.
 - Revenue: Consolidated revenue of NOK 302m (130m) and proportionate revenue
of NOK 349m (158m).
 - EBITDA: Consolidated EBITDA of NOK 160m (143m) and proportionate EBITDA of
NOK 165m (36m).
 - Production: Proportionate production of 295 GWh over the quarter (177
GWh).
 - Higher prices: Realized an average net power price of NOK 0.93 per kWh
(NOK 0.61 per kWh) compared to the Nordic system price of NOK 0.81 per kWh over
the quarter.
Highlights during the quarter
 - Transformative acquisition establishes Cloudberry as a leading Nordic IPP:
Completed the acquisition of Orrön Energy's Nordic renewable energy platform,
creating a larger, more diversified power producer with 2.1 TWh of annual
proportionate production across all Nordic price areas.
 - Signed powered land development agreement: Signed an agreement with Winn
Eiendom to develop a large-scale powered land project in Selbu, Norway with
potential gross capacity of more than 200 MW.
 - Commissioned three assets (total of 15 MW) and reached FID on one new BESS
project (8 MW), demonstrating strong execution across hydro and battery storage
projects.
 - New service agreement at Odal: Entered into a new 10-year support agreement
with Siemens Gamesa at the Odal wind farm, ensuring the basis for stable and
predictable long-term operation.

title: Cadeler signs firm contract to support turbine installation at Dogger Bank C
body:
Copenhagen, 4 November 2026 - Cadeler has signed a firm contract to support the transportation and installation of turbines at Dogger Bank C in the UK, the third 1.2GW phase of the world's largest offshore wind farm in construction. Cadeler's newbuild installation vessel, Wind Apex, will join the turbine installation campaign from Q3 2027, marking her first deployment following delivery from the shipyard.
The 3.6GW Dogger Bank Wind Farm is being built in three equal 1.2GW phases: Dogger Bank A, B and C. When complete, the project will be capable of generating enough renewable electricity to power around six million UK homes annually. 
Under the contract, Wind Apex will work alongside the project's existing installation vessel to provide additional vessel capacity to support the transportation and installation of Dogger Bank C's 87 offshore wind turbines. Wind Apex will also be available to deploy across the remaining phases of the Dogger Bank project. 
Wind Apex is the third vessel in Cadeler's A-class series, following Wind Ally and Wind Ace. The A-class vessels are designed to support both foundation and turbine installation campaigns and combine a high deck load with one of the industry's highest crane capacities. This enables the efficient installation of the latest generation of offshore wind foundations and their turbines.
Supporting one of the world's largest offshore wind developments
Dogger Bank C is the third phase of the wider 3.6 GW Dogger Bank Wind Farm, a joint venture between SSE (40%), Equinor (40%) and Vårgrønn (20%). Located approximately 130 kilometres off the north-east coast of England, SSE is leading development and construction on behalf of the three joint venture partners, while Equinor will operate the wind farm on completion for its expected operational life of around 35 years.
Cadeler has previously worked with SSE on the Beatrice and Seagreen offshore wind farms in the UK and will also work for the Equinor-partnered Bałtyk 2 and Bałtyk 3 offshore wind projects in Poland. 
Mikkel Gleerup, CEO of Cadeler, comments: "Dogger Bank is one of the world's most ambitious offshore wind developments, and we are proud to support its delivery. We value the long-standing relationships we have built with our customers and see these contracts as a reflection of the trust they place in Cadeler to execute large-scale offshore wind projects safely and efficiently. The campaign will also mark the first deployment of Wind Apex, and we look forward to seeing her begin operations on a project of this scale." 
Alan Borland, Turbine Director at Dogger Bank Wind Farm, said:
"Securing additional specialist vessel capacity for Dogger Bank C is another important step in the delivery of this world-leading offshore wind project.
Wind Apex will join the campaign as an additional turbine installation vessel, working alongside the project's existing installation vessel to safely and efficiently install Dogger Bank C's 87 turbines and support the completion of the remaining phases of the project.
Together with our partners and contractors, we remain focused on the safe delivery of all three phases of Dogger Bank and the homegrown renewable energy the wind farm will provide for the UK."
***

Cadeler A/S (Cadeler) is a global leader in offshore wind turbine transport and installation. title: Delårsregnskap 3.kvartal 2026
category: ADDITIONAL REGULATED INFORMATION REQUIRED TO BE DISCLOSED UNDER THE LAWS OF A MEMBER STATE
body:
Den gode utlånsveksten har fortsatt gjennom kvartalet. Sammen med den spennende nyheten om intensjonsavtale med Romerike Sparebank er dette et tydelig bevis på at banken fortsetter sin utvikling både gjennom organisk og strategisk vekst. I tillegg gir den positive utviklingen av verdien i Eika Gruppen en positiv effekt i utvidet resultat. 
Resultatregnskap
-God underliggende vekst
-Økte renteinntekter
-Negativ verdiendring på finansielle instrumenter
-Positiv utvikling på eierandelen i Eika Gruppen over utvidet resultat
Skue Sparebank har pr. 30.09.2026 et resultat før skatt på 321,7. mill.kroner. Dette er en økning på 22,4 mill. kroner (7,5%) mot samme periode i fjor. Sammenligningstallene mot fjoråret er påvirket av fusjonen med Tinn Sparebank som ble gjennomført 03.11.2025. Engangskostnader knyttet til fusjoner er 16,2 mill. kroner hittil i 2026. Som nevnt i forrige kvartalsrapport er alle fusjonskostnader knyttet til fusjonen med Tinn Sparebank kostnadsført. I 3.kvartal er det kostnadsført 0,2 mill. kroner knyttet til fusjonsarbeidet med Romerike Sparebank. Gjennomføringen av en juridisk og teknisk fusjon med Romerike Sparebank er forventet å koste omkring 55 MNOK. Samtidig vil den sammenslåtte banken ha en målsetning om å realisere årlige besparelser på mellom 40 - 60 MNOK når disse er fullt innfaset.
Etter skatt er det ordinære resultatet pr. 30.09.2026 på 257,4 mill. kroner som tilsvarer en egenkapitalavkastning uten hybridkapital på 8,7 %. 
Oppskrivningen av aksjer over utvidet resultat utgjør 98,1 mill. kroner hittil i år, slik at bankens totalresultat pr. 30.09.2026 er på 355,4 mill. kroner, en økning på 73,2 mill. kroner sammenlignet med fjoråret. 
Egenkapitalavkastningen av totalresultatet er 12,2% pr 30.09.2026, sammenlignet med 12,1% i fjor.
For øvrige kommentarer til delårsregnskapet vises det til vedlagte delårsrapport for 3. kvartal 2026, samt presentasjon. 
Det vil også være mulig å følge bankens presentasjon på morgendagens kapitalmarkedsdag på web med følgende link: https://qcnl.tv/p/B9j3Bo080pnunhFcfHjteg

Torgeir Nøkleby, Finansdirektør, tlf: 909 50 211, e-post: tn@skuesparebank.no

title: Wilh. Wilhelmsen Holding ASA: Third quarter 2026 results
body:
Solid performance from the operating businesses delivered an EBITDA of USD 61 million in the third quarter. Combined with continued positive contribution from associates, this resulted in a net profit of USD 155 million for the period. 
Total income for the group was USD 327 million, up 5% from the corresponding period last year, and up 2% from the second quarter of 2026. EBITDA ended at USD 61 million, up 47% from the corresponding period last year and down 2% from the previous quarter.
"Solid performance across our operating businesses continued in the quarter, and contributions from key strategic investments further supported the result. While uncertainty persists, we remain focused on maintaining resilience and financial flexibility, enabling us to perform through cycles and volatility while continuing to execute our long-term strategy," says Thomas Wilhelmsen, Group CEO.
The Maritime Services segment had a total income of USD 238 million in the third quarter. This was up 7% from the corresponding period last year and up 4% from the previous quarter. 
Total income for the New Energy segment was USD 88 million, which was stable year-over-year, but down 4% from the previous quarter. 
The Strategic Holdings and Investments segment reported a profit of USD 126 million in the third quarter. This was slightly down from the corresponding period last year, but up from previous quarter, driven by higher share of profits from Wallenius Wilhelmsen and Hyundai Glovis.
Net profit to equity holders of the company after financial items and tax was USD 154 million, equal to USD 3.70 earnings per share (EPS).
A second dividend of NOK 8.50 per share will be paid on 19 November. This comes in addition to the first dividend of NOK 20.00 per share paid in May, and is in line with the targeted long-term dividend yield of 3-5%.
Commenting on the outlook for the group, Wilhelmsen says:
"Considerable uncertainty persists, specifically regarding geopolitical tension, the ongoing conflict in the Middle East, and an uncertain global trade environment, potentially impacting future performance and cash inflow. However, the group retains its capacity to support, grow, and expand the business portfolio, and to deliver yearly dividends in line with the dividend policy."

title: AutoStore to acquire Logiqs
body:
(Nedre Vats, November 5, 2026): AutoStore Holdings Ltd. (AutoStore,
OSE:AUTO),announced an agreement to acquire Logiqs BV ("Logiqs"), a provider of
roaming pallet Automated Storage and Retrieval Systems (AS/RS), for a purchase
price of up to EUR 30 million.
"This acquisition is another step in our journey towards building an autonomous,
intelligent fulfilment platform. In Logiqs, we have identified a core technology
that, over time, will bring roaming pallet AS/RS into the AutoStore platform,
helping us address a broader set of needs for both new and existing customers",
said Mats Hovland Vikse, CEO of AutoStore.
Based in the Netherlands, Logiqs develops roaming robots for the automated
storage and retrieval of palletized goods. Its warehouse technology is deployed
at approximately 30 customer sites across multiple geographies and end markets,
helping customers improve storage density, throughput and operational
efficiency. Logiqs' 60 employees bring complementary automation, software and
product capabilities to AutoStore.
"For Logiqs, this is an opportunity to accelerate our technology together with
AutoStore. I am confident that the combined expertise of Logiqs and AutoStore
will create value for our customers. The cultural similarities between our two
companies are a great starting point for a successful collaboration going
forward", said Reyer van der Louw, CEO of Logiqs
 "During the process, we've been impressed with Logiqs' deep experience and
insight into what is an exciting new product and technology area for us. We look
forward to working together to further develop the platform and create value for
customers", said Parth Joshi, Chief Product Officer and President Product
Business Unit at AutoStore.
The purchase price will be funded from existing cash reserves and is not
expected to have a material impact on AutoStore's financial results. Additional
information will be provided over time, as AutoStore further develops the
technology in preparation for expanded commercial release.
The transaction is expected to close in Q4 2026, subject to customary closing
conditions.

body:
Oslo, 2026-11-05
Quarterly highlights[1]:
* Investments of NOK 772m and NOK 3.7bn invested and committed for 2026
* Unsecured collection performance of 112%
* Opex of NOK 431m, down 4% with 10% growth in unsecured collections
* Cash EBITDA of NOK 1,080m, up 6%
* Underlying cost of debt down 10% 
* Net profit of NOK 234m, up 44%

Increased financial targets for 2026:
- EPS above NOK 2.40
- ROE of ~17%

Excluding non-recurring items.
Collections remained strong in the third quarter with an unsecured collection
performance of 112%, up from 108% in the same quarter last year.
Cash collections on a comparable basis were up 6% adjusted for the sale of one
large REO position in the third quarter last year. Cash EBITDA was NOK 1,080
million and EBIT was NOK 489 million. Net profit was NOK 234 million
equivalent to earnings per share of NOK 0.63, up 27% in constant FX. Adjusted
for the large REO sale in Q3 2025, growth in earnings per share was 44%.
B2 Impact invested NOK 772 million in new portfolios in the third quarter. The
investments in the quarter were unsecured and mixed portfolios. The Estimated
Remaining Collections (ERC) were NOK 27 billion representing a 19% growth on a
comparable basis. ERC including REOs were NOK 28 billion. As of today, the
Group has invested and committed NOK 3.7 billion for 2026 in constant FX.
B2 Impact has a solid and diversified funding structure. In August, the Group
signed a renegotiated 3-year RCF of EUR 510m with DNB and Nordea at improved
terms, with a 2-year extension option. In September, the Group issued a new
bond of EUR 150m with a 2.65% margin over 3m EURIBOR with maturity in 2032.
The Group holds four senior unsecured bond loans for a total of EUR 800
million. The liquidity reserve at the end of the quarter was around EUR 335
million. The leverage ratio at the end of the third quarter was 2.3x.
"We experienced high investment activity in the third quarter, with growth of
15% in portfolio investments versus the same quarter last year. We expect high
seasonal activity for portfolio investments in the fourth quarter, and we
enter the quarter in a very strong position where we can be selective and
price disciplined. We maintain the investment target for the full-year of NOK
4bn.
I am pleased to see the strong development of the company year-to-date. With
our revised targets for 2026 we are well positioned to once again deliver
value to our shareholders through attractive dividends while at the same time
maintaining sustainable growth and a healthy balance sheet." says Trond
Kristian Andreassen, CEO of B2 Impact ASA.

title: Moreld ASA: Third quarter 2026 results
body:
Stavanger, 5 November 2026: Moreld delivered another strong quarter with
revenues of NOK 2.2 billion and adjusted EBITDA of NOK 376 million,
corresponding to an EBITDA margin of 17 per cent. The result was driven by
high vessel utilisation and strong project performance in Ocean Installer.
With improved visibility for the remainder of the year, Moreld raises its
full-year 2026 EBITDA guidance to NOK 0.85-1.0 billion.
"We delivered another strong quarter, driven by excellent project execution in
Ocean Installer, demonstrating the earnings potential in our subsea business.
Combined with a strong backlog, low net debt and improved visibility into 2027
and beyond, this gives us confidence to raise our full-year guidance while
continuing to return capital to shareholders," says CEO Geir Austigard.
Supported by a strong balance sheet and solid cash position, the board of
directors reconfirmed the ambition to maintain predictable quarterly dividends
and approved a dividend of NOK 0.50 per share for distribution in November. In
addition, the board approved a new share buyback programme of up to 5 million
shares, with the purpose of reducing the company's share capital.
Highlights
* Strong third quarter with revenue of NOK 2.2 billion and adjusted EBITDA of
 NOK 376 million, representing a 17 per cent margin, supported by strong
 execution and project milestones
* Highest quarterly adjusted EBITDA margin since listing, driven by
 exceptional execution in Ocean Installer, while Moreld Apply continues to
 reposition for future opportunities
* Organisation and cost base continue to be adjusted to current activity
 levels
* Pursuing new project awards and opportunities across core and adjacent
 markets
* Order intake of approximately NOK 1.8 billion in the quarter strengthens
 Ocean Installer's position in key subsea growth markets
* Order backlog was NOK 8.1 billion at quarter-end, providing improved
 visibility into 2027 and beyond
* Balance sheet remains strong with a cash balance of NOK 1.2 billion and a
 leverage ratio of 0.1x at the end of the quarter
* Full-year 2026 EBITDA guidance raised from NOK 0.7-0.9 billion to NOK
 0.85-1.0 billion, reflecting strong year-to-date performance and improved
 visibility entering the fourth quarter
Profit distribution to shareholders
* Dividend of NOK 0.50 per share distributed in August
* A further NOK 0.50 per share dividend approved by the board for distribution
 in November
* New share buyback programme of up to 5 million shares, representing
 approximately 2.8 per cent of outstanding shares and a maximum consideration
 of NOK 100 million, approved with the purpose of reducing the company's
 share capital

title: 3. kvartal 2026: Fortsatt resultatvekst for Polaris Media i tredje kvartal
body:
Polaris Media leverte en EBITDA justert for engangseffekter på 126 millioner
kroner i tredje kvartal 2026, en forbedring på 23 millioner kroner fra samme
periode i fjor. Justert EBITDA-margin økte til 14 prosent, det høyeste nivået
siden tredje kvartal 2021. Resultatveksten var drevet av sterk digital
inntektsutvikling og effekter fra kostnadstiltak i Sverige.
- Det er særlig gledelig at inntektsveksten i de svenske mediehusene
fortsetter etter at utviklingen snudde i andre kvartal. Vårt målrettede arbeid
med å styrke de digitale produktene gir resultater. Også i Norge har vi god
vekst i brukerinntektene, selv om annonsemarkedet fortsatt er krevende, sier
konsernsjef Per Axel Koch.
Sterk resultatvekst i Sverige
Mediehusene i Stampen Media mer enn doblet justert EBITDA til 46 millioner
kroner, opp fra 22 millioner kroner i tredje kvartal i fjor. Målt i lokal
valuta økte brukerinntektene med sju prosent og annonseinntektene med 15
prosent. Dette var andre kvartal på rad med vekst i begge inntektsstrømmene.
De norske mediehusene leverte en EBITDA på 78 millioner kroner, mot 82
millioner kroner i samme periode i fjor. Brukerinntektene økte med seks
prosent, men nedgang i annonseinntektene ga et noe svakere resultat.
- I Sverige bidrar både inntektsvekst og en lavere kostnadsbase til
resultatfremgangen. De norske mediehusene har over tid hatt solid vekst i
brukerinntektene. Jeg er meget fornøyd med innsatsen til mediehusene våre i
begge land. Gjennom sterk lokal og regional journalistikk gir de folk innsikt
i det som skjer der de bor, og setter viktige saker på dagsordenen. Et godt
eksempel er Adresseavisens "Kloakkavsløringen", som i oktober ble hedret på ny
med diplom under Data-SKUP, sier Koch.
Flere digitale abonnenter
Digitale brukerinntekter økte med 14 prosent i Norge og 22 prosent i Sverige,
målt i lokal valuta. Veksten var drevet av flere heldigitale abonnement og
høyere inntekt per abonnement. I Sverige har GP Medlem og en tydeligere
differensiering av abonnementstilbudet vært sentrale tiltak for å løfte
inntektene.
Ved utgangen av kvartalet var antallet heldigitale abonnement i konsernet tre
prosent høyere enn på samme tid i fjor, mens antallet fullprisbetalende økte
med seks prosent. Heldigitale abonnement utgjorde 76 prosent av konsernets
samlede abonnementsbase.
- Veksten i fullprisbetalende digitale abonnenter er viktig for å bygge varige
brukerinntekter. Vi fortsetter å investere i journalistikk, produktutvikling
og teknologi som gjør tilbudet mer relevant og verdifullt for brukerne, sier
Koch.
Ulik utvikling i annonseinntektene
De svenske mediehusenes annonseinntekter økte med 15 prosent målt i lokal
valuta, drevet av 29 prosent vekst i digitale annonseinntekter. Riksdagsvalget
i september bidro til veksten, men de digitale annonseinntektene har vist
solid fremgang siden tredje kvartal 2025. I Norge ble annonseinntektene
redusert med 11 prosent, med en nedgang på seks prosent digitalt og 20 prosent
på papir.
- Våre svenske mediehus fortsatte den sterke veksten i digitale
annonseinntekter. I Norge var det generelt et svakt annonsekvartal for
nyhetsmediene. Vi fortsetter arbeidet med å styrke konkurransekraften for å få
tilbake veksten i de digitale annonseinntektene i Norge, kommenterer Koch.
Fortsatt effekt av kostnadstiltak
Konsernets driftskostnader justert for engangseffekter ble redusert med tre
prosent fra tredje kvartal i fjor. Nedgangen var i hovedsak drevet av de
betydelige kostnadstiltakene som ble gjennomført i Stampen Media i tredje
kvartal 2025.
- Tiltakene i Stampen Media var en nødvendig tilpasning av kostnadene i både
mediehusene og distribusjonsvirksomheten som nå gir god effekt. Samtidig viser
virksomhetene i Norge god kostnadsdisiplin. Jeg er særlig tilfreds med jobben
trykkeri- og distribusjonsvirksomheten gjør med løpende effektivisering og
tilpasning til fallende papirvolumer, slik at de opprettholder gode
resultater, sier Koch.
Foreløpig gjennomslag mot Meta
Oslo tingrett ga 28. oktober Polaris Media og en samlet norsk mediebransje
medhold i kravet om å stanse Metas nye kommersielle vilkår. Tingretten forbyr
Meta å iverksette endring av vilkårene inntil lovligheten av endringen er
rettskraftig avgjort.
- Vi er glade for at vi har fått medhold i denne prinsipielt viktige saken.
Vilkårene kunne gitt Meta vid adgang til å bruke de redaktørstyrte medienes
innhold uten særskilt avtale eller betaling, sier Koch.

title: Selvaag Bolig ASA: Q3 2026: Increased earnings and record-high sales value
body:
Selvaag Bolig sold 625 homes net for NOK 4.5 billion during the first nine
months of the year. The company has thereby already exceeded its previous
full-year sales record of NOK 4.3 billion from 2016. EBITDA adjusted for
financial expenses, including the company's share in joint venture projects,
increased to NOK 239 million in the third quarter, compared with NOK 90
million in the same period last year.
In the third quarter, Selvaag Bolig sold 95 homes net with a sales value of
NOK 643 million. During the same period, 186 homes were delivered to buyers,
compared with 98 in the same period last year.
So far this year, Selvaag Bolig has started construction of 575 homes and
delivered 397 homes to buyers. At the end of the third quarter, Selvaag Bolig
had 1 019 homes under construction with a combined sales value of NOK 7.2
billion. Of these, 64 percent were sold. Of the homes expected to be completed
in 2026, 74 percent were sold. The company had 93 completed unsold homes at
the end of the period.
"We are pleased with the increased earnings and with having exceeded our
previous full-year record in sales value in just nine months. This indicates
that our projects and housing concepts meet buyers' needs. However, the market
remains challenging. Buyers' purchasing power is under pressure, and high
construction and financing costs make it more difficult to launch new
projects. The number of completed unsold homes has also increased," says CEO
Sverre Molvik.
In the third quarter, Selvaag Bolig started construction of the first 119
homes at Terrasskvarteret Pluss in Stockholm. The project comprises a total of
166 homes, and binding purchase agreements have been signed for more than 65
percent of the project's total sales value.
"The construction start of Terrasskvarteret Pluss marks an important milestone
for our operations in Sweden. We also see an improvement in Central
Stockholm's housing market, with rising house prices and increased activity,
although buyers remain selective. In total, we have more than 1 000 homes
under construction in Norway and Sweden, and we are pleased with the level of
activity in a market that remains challenging," Molvik continues.
