title: Selvaag Bolig ASA: Q3 2026: Resultatvekst og rekordhøy salgsverdi
body:
Selvaag Bolig solgte netto 625 boliger for 4,5 milliarder kroner i årets
første ni måneder. Dermed har selskapet allerede passert sin tidligere
helårsrekord på 4,3 milliarder kroner fra 2016. EBITDA justert for
finanskostnader, inkludert selskapets andel i samarbeidsprosjekter, økte til
239 millioner kroner i tredje kvartal, mot 90 millioner kroner i samme periode
i fjor.
I tredje kvartal solgte Selvaag Bolig netto 95 boliger med en salgsverdi på
643 millioner kroner. Samtidig ble 186 boliger overlevert, mot 98 i samme
periode i fjor.
Hittil i år har Selvaag Bolig igangsatt bygging av 575 boliger og overlevert
397 boliger til kjøperne. Ved utgangen av tredje kvartal hadde Selvaag Bolig 1
019 boliger under bygging, med en samlet salgsverdi på 7,2 milliarder kroner.
Av disse var 64 prosent solgt. Av boligene som er forventet ferdigstilt i
2026, var 74 prosent solgt. Ved utgangen av perioden hadde selskapet
93 ferdigstilte, usolgte boliger.
-- Vi er fornøyde med resultatveksten og at vi allerede etter ni måneder har
passert vår tidligere årsrekord i salgsverdi. Det tyder på at prosjektene og
boligkonseptene våre treffer kjøpernes behov. Markedet er likevel fortsatt
krevende. Kjøpernes økonomi er presset, og høye bygge- og finanskostnader gjør
det vanskeligere å realisere nye prosjekter. Beholdningen av ferdigstilte,
usolgte boliger har også økt, sier administrerende direktør Sverre Molvik.
I tredje kvartal startet Selvaag Bolig byggingen av de første 119 boligene i
Terrasskvarteret Pluss i Stockholm. Prosjektet omfatter totalt 166 boliger, og
det er inngått bindende kjøpsavtaler for mer enn 65 prosent av prosjektet
samlede salgsverdi.
-- Byggestarten på Terrasskvarteret Pluss er en viktig milepæl for satsingen
vår i Sverige. Vi ser samtidig bedring i boligmarkedet i sentrale Stockholm,
med stigende boligpriser og økt aktivitet, selv om kjøperne fortsatt er
selektive. Samlet har vi over 1 000 boliger under bygging i Norge og Sverige,
og vi er fornøyde med aktivitetsnivået i et fortsatt krevende marked,
fortsetter Molvik.

title: Moreld ASA: Launch of share buy-back programme
category: ACQUISITION OR DISPOSAL OF AN ISSUER'S OWN SHARES
body:
Stavanger, 5 November 2026: The Board of Directors of Moreld ASA ("Moreld" or
the "Company") has resolved to launch a share buy-back programme (the
"Programme"), pursuant to the authorisation granted by the annual general
meeting on 19 May 2026.
The purpose of the Programme is to reduce the Company's share capital. Shares
acquired under the Programme will be proposed cancelled at a subsequent
general meeting.
Under the Programme, the Company may acquire up to 5,000,000 shares,
representing approximately 2.8 % of the outstanding shares, for a maximum
total amount of NOK 100 million. The Programme will commence on 5 November
2026 and end no later than 30 June 2027, when the authorisation expires. The
Company is not obliged to acquire any shares under the Programme and may
terminate it early.
The Programme will be carried out in accordance with Regulation (EU) No
596/2014 (MAR) Article 5 and Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) No
2016/1052.
Moreld has engaged SB1 Markets AS to manage and carry out the share
repurchases in the market, and SB1 Markets AS will make its trading decisions
independently of the Company. 
As of the date of this announcement, the Company holds 2,674,406 treasury
shares, out of a total of 179,555,119 shares issued.

This information is made public by the Company pursuant to MAR and is subject
to the disclosure requirements pursuant to section 5-12 of the Norwegian
Securities Trading Act.

title: Napatech A/S: Q3 2026 Financial Results
body:
(Copenhagen, 5 November 2026) Napatech A/S ("Napatech", OSE: NAPA) reported
revenues of USD 10.3 million in Q3 2026, corresponding to DKK 66.9 million,
representing 64% growth in USD and 67% growth in DKK compared to Q3 2025. A
growth of 39% quarter-over-quarter and the highest third quarter revenue in
Napatech history. Gross margin for the quarter was 55.4%. This was due to a
one-time temporary lag in repricing of the initial ramp order within AI
Infrastructure. A revised pricing structure takes effect in Q4 improving our
gross margin considerably, supporting our unchanged full-year revenue and
gross-margin guidance.
The company's EBITDA in Q3 2026 improved to close to break-even from negative
DKK 6.1 million in Q3 2025. Cash flow from operating activities was negative
DKK 15.3 million in Q3 2026, primarily impacted by backloaded invoicing. Net
working capital at quarter-end amounted to DKK 116.1 million, reflecting
backloaded invoicing and higher inventories. Cash and cash equivalents
amounted to DKK 45.5 million, with total available liquidity of DKK 67.1
million, including undrawn committed facilities.
The third quarter of 2026 marked an important milestone in Napatech's
transformation, with our first AI Infrastructure production shipments
complementing continued Core Infrastructure growth. This represents tangible
progress in translating our AI strategy into commercial results.
With a strong Core business and AI Infrastructure entering commercial
production, Napatech is positioned for its next phase of growth. The focus
remains on scaling customer programs, converting opportunities into revenue,
and delivering sustainable, profitable growth. Based on current performance
and visibility, the company maintains its financial guidance for 2026
unchanged:

+------------------------------------------------+----------------------------+

title: Kid ASA - Third Quarter 2026 Results
body:
Lier, 5 November 2026: Kid Group, a leading home and interior retailer in the
Nordics, announces its financial results for the third quarter of 2026.
HIGHLIGHTS FOR THE QUARTER INCLUDE:
 - Group revenues increased by 12.3% to MNOK 1,012.7 (15.2% in constant
currency), supported by solid growth across both Kid Interior and Hemtex and
strong seasonal assortments
 - Gross margin increased by 0.5 percentage points to 62.3% (61.8%), supported
by favourable currency effects
 - OPEX decreased by 0.6% (+12.0%), with higher activity levels, investments in
systems and bonus, offset by currency effects and non-recurring items Q3 2025
 - EBITDA increased by 38.5% to MNOK 283.5 (MNOK 204.7), up MNOK 78.8 year-over
-year
 - EPS increased by NOK 1.37 to NOK 2.35 (NOK 0.98), mainly reflecting the
improved operating result and non-recurring items in the comparison period
 - Operating cash flow improved by MNOK 167.6 compared with Q3 2025, supported
by improved working capital development and higher profitability
 - Half-year dividend payment NOK 2.75 (NOK 2.50) per share as a prepayment for
the fiscal year 2026, payable in November
"Kid Group delivered strong and broad-based revenue growth in the third quarter,
with solid performance across both segments and major product categories.
Warehouse operations are stable, product availability is good and our focus is
increasingly on efficiency and productivity improvements. Together with strong
assortments, this leaves us well prepared for the important Christmas shopping
season" says Marianne Fulford, CEO of Kid ASA.

Rogaland Sparebank med godt resultat og fortsatt vekst
body:
Rogaland Sparebank oppnådde et resultat etter skatt på 397,9 millioner kroner for de tre første kvartalene i 2026, mot 390,6 millioner kroner i samme periode i 2025.
Egenkapitalavkastningen etter skatt, inkludert renteutgifter på hybridkapital, ble 12,1 prosent (12,5 prosent) for årets ni første måneder.
Rentenettoen utgjorde 560,8 millioner kroner (590,1 millioner kroner), mens andre driftsinntekter økte til 196,7 millioner kroner (181,5 millioner kroner).
Driftskostnadene ble redusert til 281,3 millioner kroner, fra 303,7 millioner kroner i samme periode i fjor. Kostnadsgraden ble 37,1 prosent (39,4 prosent).
Nedskrivninger og tap på utlån og garantier utgjorde 24,6 millioner kroner (22,4 millioner kroner).
- Vi leverer et godt resultat etter årets ni første måneder. Lavere rentemargin påvirker rentenettoen, mens reduserte driftskostnader og fortsatt lave tap bidrar positivt. Samtidig fortsetter banken å vokse i Rogaland, sier Tomas Nordbø, administrerende direktør i Rogaland Sparebank.
Fortsatt vekst i personmarkedet
Banken har passert 30 milliarder kroner i utlån til personmarkedet. Siden fusjonen mellom Hjelmeland Sparebank og Sandnes Sparebank i august 2024 har utlånene i personmarkedet økt med 4,5 milliarder kroner.
Brutto utlånsvekst de siste tolv månedene var 5,7 prosent (9,2 prosent), mens innskuddsveksten var 8,1 prosent (7,9 prosent).
- Utviklingen viser at banken fortsetter å styrke sin posisjon i Rogaland. Veksten i personmarkedet er i tråd med bankens langsiktige strategi om økte markedsandeler i regionen, sier Nordbø.
Styrket tilstedeværelse på Jæren
Som en del av bankens langsiktige vekststrategi åpnet Rogaland Sparebank nytt kontor på Bryne i august 2026.
Etableringen styrker bankens tilstedeværelse på Jæren og gir banken et bedre utgangspunkt for videre vekst i området.
- Nå har vi også åpnet på Bryne, og det gir oss et enda sterkere utgangspunkt for videre vekst på Jæren, sier Nordbø.
Den første tiden etter åpningen har vist god kundeaktivitet og positiv respons i markedet.

title: Norwegian Air Shuttle ASA (NAS) - Traffic Figures for October 2026
body:
The Norwegian Group carried 2.8 million passengers in October, of which 2.4 million travelled with Norwegian and 395,000 with Widerøe. Norwegian had a load factor of 89.2 percent in October, while Widerøe reached 75.3 percent, marking the highest October load factor in both airlines' history. Alongside record high load factors, both carriers continued to deliver world-class punctuality. 
"I am very pleased to see record high load factor for both Norwegian and Widerøe. The autumn holiday period was characterised by full flights and strong results, and I am proud of our colleagues around Europe for delivering solid punctuality during this busy travel season. Widerøe continues to uphold a world-class level in punctuality, which has become a hallmark of the operation this year," said Geir Karlsen, CEO of Norwegian. 
Norwegian's capacity (ASK) in October was 3,620 million seat kilometres, an increase of 5 percent compared with October 2025. Actual passenger traffic (RPK) was 3,229 million seat kilometres, an increase of 7 percent from the same period last year. The load factor was 89.2 percent, up 2.0 percentage points. Regularity, the share of scheduled flights that took place, was 99.5 percent. Punctuality, the share of flights departing within 15 minutes of scheduled time, was 83.7 percent. In October, Norwegian operated an average of 91 aircraft. 
"Looking ahead, booking momentum for the winter season remains encouraging with significantly more tickets sold compared to the same time last year. Christmas holiday bookings are accelerating, and for those planning to travel over Christmas, we recommend securing your tickets as early as possible," said Geir Karlsen, CEO of Norwegian.
Widerøe's capacity (ASK) was 196 million seat kilometres in October, unchanged from the previous year. Actual passenger traffic (RPK) was 147 million seat kilometres, up 3 percent from September 2025. The load factor was 75.3 percent, up 1.9 percentage points from last year. Punctuality was 93.3 percent, an increase of 4.6 percent from last year. Once again, this ranks Widerøe as one of the top airlines in the world on punctuality. Regularity was 96.8 percent in October.
"Overall, October was a very strong month for Widerøe. We continue to deliver punctuality at the very highest level, alongside achieving the highest October load factor in company history. Combined with improving booking momentum heading into the coming months, these traffic figures are promising," said Tore Jenssen, CEO of Widerøe.

Aker Solutions receives letter of award for engineering scope on the Maydan Mahzam project in Qatar
body:
November 5, 2026 - Aker Solutions has received a letter of award (LOA) from PTSC
Mechanical and Construction Limited Company (PTSC M&C) for a sizeable[1]
contract for detail design work related to the redevelopment of the Maydan
Mahzam oil field offshore Qatar.
The work will be executed by Aker Solutions' engineering teams in Kuala Lumpur,
Malaysia, and Mumbai, India.
The Maydan Mahzam oil field is located about 100 kilometres (km) northeast of
the Qatari coastline and 28 km southeast of Halul Island, in water depths of
about 40 metres. The oil field, along with the nearby Bul Hanine field, was
discovered in the 1960s and has been in production since 1965. Operator
QatarEnergy is now planning a major redevelopment project to upgrade and extend
the operational life of the field. PTSC M&C has been selected by QatarEnergy for
a key package in the redevelopment program.
Aker Solutions will provide detail design services for several offshore
installations under PTSC M&C 's project scope, including three major topsides,
four jackets and brownfield tie-in.
"This award reflects the strength of our engineering organization and our long
track record of delivering complex offshore projects. Our team in Kuala Lumpur
brings extensive offshore oil and gas experience, complemented by the
capabilities of our office in Mumbai and the wider Aker Solutions organization.
Together, we look forward to supporting the successful execution of the Maydan
Mahzam project," said Guro Rausand, Executive Vice President of New Build at
Aker Solutions.
The LOA is subject to the signing of the final contract. Upon signing, Aker
Solutions expects to book a sizeable[1] order intake in the fourth quarter of
2026 in the Renewables and Field Development segment.
[1]Aker Solutions defines a sizeable contract as being between NOK 0.5 billion
and NOK 1.5 billion.

title: Agilyx: GreenDot to acquire 50% of French packaging EPR company Léko, expanding its European recycling platform
body:
Oslo, Norway, 5 November 2026 - Agilyx ASA (Euronext Oslo Børs: AGLX; Börse Frankfurt: 5NQ; US OTCQX: AGYXY) ("Agilyx" or the "Company") announces that GreenDot, its majority-owned holding, has entered into an agreement to acquire 50% of Valorie SAS, a fast-growing state-approved extended producer responsibility (EPR) recycling company in France owning 100% of Léko and Léko Pro. GreenDot will share joint ownership and control of Valorie with German environmental services company Reclay International. The transaction is funded from cash within the GreenDot Group and involves no cash outlay and no share issuance by Agilyx.
A fast-growing challenger in French recycling
Léko is one of two state-approved, non-profit household packaging EPR organizations in France, which receives (EPR) fees brands pay to fund municipal collection, sorting and recycling. Since its start in 2020, revenue has grown to EUR 42 million in 2025, with nearly 80% annual growth in the past two years.
France generates approximately 4.5 million tonnes of plastic waste each year. In 2024, the French recycling rate for plastic packaging was only 27%, the third lowest in the EU, which averages 42%. France pays approximately EUR 1.6 billion per year to the EU related to its non-recycled plastic packaging waste and is working proactively to transform its plastic recycling sector.
Strategic rationale
The strategic expansion of GreenDot's European recycling platform is expected to create value through three channels:
- Enhanced access to more and higher-quality mechanical recycling feedstock: Léko provides GreenDot's mechanical recycling operations with preferred access to more, higher-quality material, enhancing the platform's EU Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation (PPWR)-driven growth.
- One-stop-shop for Pan-European EPR compliance: Together, Léko and GreenDot can offer brands a one-stop shop for EPR compliance in Germany and France, access to GreenDot's Authorized Representative service, and access to the AI software solution GreenDot is developing with osapiens.
- Cost savings with German EPR: Léko will leverage GreenDot's existing IT, digital tools and account teams, lowering costs in both France and Germany, particularly as Léko grows.
GreenDot's ambition is to grow Léko toward a 10% share of the French household packaging recycling market, increasing the value of each of the above.
Laurent Auguste, CEO of GreenDot, said: "Léko's presence in the French waste plastic supply chain provides GreenDot a strategic opportunity to expand our access to waste plastic supply and advance our circular plastics offering to pan-European brands and retailers. Our teams have been working together for some time now, and I am excited about building Leko into a central player in the French recycling segment. "
Transaction terms
GreenDot will pay an initial consideration of EUR 4 million at closing. The agreement also provides for two potential milestone payments, dependent on Leko's revenue growth. Milestone payments are voided if the anticipated synergies are not achievable due to regulatory constraints. Total consideration, including milestone payments, is approximately 2-3 times GreenDot's projected annual EBITDA improvement and is capped at three times the initial consideration.
The acquisition is funded from cash within the GreenDot Group. There is no cash outlay and no share issuance by Agilyx. Léko will not be consolidated in GreenDot's accounts.
As part of the new ownership structure, GreenDot CEO Laurent Auguste will assume the role of Chairman of Valorie. The transaction was completed on November 5th 2026.
Further details are provided in the enclosed attachment.
About Agilyx
Agilyx ASA is a leading global investment platform supporting the development of plastic waste feedstock supply to the recycling industry. Through its majority holding in GreenDot Global, Europe's largest waste plastic recycling platform, Agilyx has access to large volumes of post-use plastic and advanced sorting and recycling infrastructure in Austria, France, Germany, Italy, and Spain. Through arcLABS, Agilyx provides characterization and identification services for plastic streams that can be converted into feedstock matched to recycling processes. Agilyx also markets Styrenyx, its proprietary chemical recycling technology for polystyrene waste.
By enabling the shift from a linear "make-take-waste" model to a circular economy, Agilyx helps solve the plastic waste crisis and supports the global transition to a low-carbon future.
Inquiries: investors@agilyx.com
Learn more at: www.agilyx.com and www.agilyx.com/arclabs
For media resources, visit: https://www.agilyx.com/media-room/
About GreenDot
GreenDot is dedicated to addressing the plastic waste crisis by developing solutions and assets that close the circularity loop of plastics through the production of high-quality recyclates, including from difficult-to-recycle waste streams. The group's portfolio spans both mechanical and chemical recycling, Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) licensing services, as well as consulting on EPR systems and design-for-recycling.
The foundation of the group was laid more than 35 years ago in Germany with Der Grüne Punkt, which created the world's first nationwide EPR program for household packaging, including hard-to-recycle plastics like flexible films. Since then, GreenDot has constantly expanded its business areas in order to serve all requirements of the circular economy for plastics. To date, GreenDot has a presence in Germany, Austria, Italy, France, as well as Spain, and continues to widen its global network.
More information can be found at www.green-dot.com

CAPITAL TANKERS CORP. ANNOUNCES A TIME CHARTER FOR THE DUAL FUEL SUEZMAX TANKER M/T AMOR
body:
ATHENS, Greece, November 6, 2026 -- Capital Tankers Corp. (the "Company",
"CAPT", "we" or "us"), an international shipping company focused on crude oil
transportation, today announced a time charter employment for the dual fuel
Suezmax tanker M/T Amor.
The Company has entered into a 15-month time charter agreement for the M/T
Amor (155,348 DWT, Dual Fuel LNG capable, scrubber-fitted, built 2026, New
Times Shipbuilding Co., Ltd., China) with a global energy company. The
charter, which remains subject to the charterer's vetting approval, commenced
in November 2026 and is expected to generate revenues of between $73.1 million
and $82.2 million.
About Capital Tankers Corp.
Capital Tankers Corp. (Euronext Growth Oslo: CAPT) is a Marshall
Islands-incorporated owner of modern crude and product tankers trading its
vessels predominantly in the spot and short-term charter markets. The Company
owns a fleet of 33 latest generation eco vessels --- 15 VLCCs, 10 Suezmax and
eight Aframax/LR2 tankers --- comprising 17 sailing vessels and 16
newbuildings scheduled for delivery between 2027 and 2028, with options for 13
additional crude tankers. 23 of the 33 vessels are dual-fuel LNG ready or
capable, providing the Company with significant potential fuel and regulatory
cost advantages. For further information please visit www.capitaltankers.com

title: Orkla rapporterer resultater for tredje kvartal
body:
Orklas konsoliderte porteføljeselskaper (inkludert Orkla ASA) leverte en vekst
i underliggende EBIT (adj.) på 8,1 % i tredje kvartal. EBIT (adj.) for
Orkla-konsernet utgjorde 2,1 mrd. kroner, en økning på 1,9 %. Forskjellen i
vekst skyldes i hovedsak en sterkere krone.
De konsoliderte porteføljeselskapene hadde en organisk vekst på 3,1 %.
Volum/miks-veksten utgjorde 2,7 %, og de fleste porteføljeselskapene bidro.
Orklas driftsinntekter endte på 17,5 mrd. kroner. 
Resultatbidraget fra Jotun var 563 mill. kroner, en nedgang på 6,6 %. Jotun
hadde en vekst i salget på 13 % og i driftsresultatet på 1,3 %, justert for
negative valutaomregningseffekter. 
Resultat per aksje (adj.) var 1,94 kroner i kvartalet, opp 4,9 % sammenlignet
med samme periode i fjor, som følge av vekst i EBIT (adj.) i de konsoliderte
porteføljeselskapene og tilbakekjøp av egne aksjer. 
I september startet Orkla et nytt program for tilbakekjøp av egne aksjer på
inntil 4 mrd. kroner. Programmet løper senest til 31. desember 2027. Samme
måned gjennomførte Orkla Snacks kjøpet av The European Candy Group, for å
støtte den videre veksten til BUBS. 
-- Vi leverte et godt tredje kvartal med volumvekst og bredbasert fremgang på
tvers av porteføljen. Jeg er særlig fornøyd med bidraget fra Orkla Snacks.
Orkla har nå levert vekst i underliggende EBIT (adj.) i samtlige kvartaler i
strategiperioden. Vi ser frem til kapitalmarkedsdagen 1. desember, der vi vil
presentere nye mål og ambisjoner for perioden frem til 2030, sier konsernsjef
Nils K. Selte i Orkla. 
Om Orkla
Orkla ASA er et ledende industrielt investeringsselskap innen merkevarer og
forbrukerorienterte virksomheter, med 10 porteføljeselskaper. Selskapet har en
langsiktig og strategisk tilnærming til investeringer, og skaper verdi ved å
kombinere merkevarekompetanse med tankesettet til et investeringsselskap.
Orkla er notert på Oslo Børs og har hovedkontor i Oslo, Norge. Orkla hadde en
omsetning på 71,5 mrd. kroner i 2025.

title: Orkla reports results for the third quarter
body:
Orkla's consolidated portfolio companies (including Orkla ASA) delivered
underlying EBIT (adj.) growth of 8.1% in the third quarter. EBIT (adj.) for
the Orkla group amounted to 2.1 billion, an increase of 1.9%. The difference
in growth is mainly explained by a stronger Norwegian krone.
The consolidated portfolio companies delivered organic revenue growth of 3.1%.
Volume/mix growth accounted for 2.7%, with most of the portfolio companies
contributing. Orkla's operating revenues amounted to 17.5 billion.
Profit from Jotun was 563 million, a decline of 6.6%. Jotun's sales growth was
13% and operating profit growth was 1.3%, adjusted for negative currency
translation effects.
Earnings per share (adj.) for the quarter was NOK 1.94, up 4.9% compared to
the same period last year, driven by EBIT (adj.) growth in the consolidated
portfolio companies and share repurchases.
In September, Orkla initiated a new share buyback programme of up to 4
billion, which will run until 31 December 2027 at the latest. In the same
month, Orkla Snacks completed its acquisition of The European Candy Group, to
support the continued growth of BUBS.
"We delivered a good third quarter with volume growth and broad-based progress
across the portfolio. Orkla has now delivered underlying EBIT (adj.) growth in
every quarter of the strategy period. We look forward to our Capital Markets
Day on 1 December, where we will present new targets and ambitions for the
period to 2030," says Orkla President and CEO Nils K. Selte.
About Orkla
Orkla ASA is a leading industrial investment company within brands and
consumer-oriented businesses, with 10 portfolio companies. The company takes a
long-term and strategic approach to its investments, creating value by
combining brand expertise with an investment company mindset. Orkla is listed
on the Oslo Stock Exchange and is headquartered in Oslo, Norway. Orkla had a
turnover of 71.5 billion in 2025.

title: Hexagon Composites ASA: Third quarter 2026
body:
6 November 2026: Hexagon Composites (OSE: HEX.OL), world leader in composite
cylinder technology and related systems for storage and transportation of
gaseous energy, reported revenues of NOK 929 million for third quarter 2026
(Q3'25: 538 million). The reported EBITDA was NOK 108 million (Q3'25: NOK -54
million), resulting in a 12% EBITDA margin (Q3'25: -10%).
"This quarter marks a significant step-up year-over-year, delivering our
strongest quarterly performance since the record fourth quarter of 2024," said
Philipp Schramm, CEO of Hexagon Composites. "Over the past year, we have built a
stronger foundation for our next phase of growth. We have entered new regions,
consolidated markets and delivered into exciting new verticals such as aerospace
and data centers. Alongside this important progress, we have also improved our
financial strength, with a strong free cash flow conversion, and are well on
track to deliver on our full-year targets."
Outlook
Based on the progress delivered during the first three quarters of the year, the
strengthening of our financial position, and normalizing demand in our key
markets, we reconfirm our full-year EBITDA guidance of around NOK 300 million,
with confidence in delivering toward the high side.
For further details, please see the attached third quarter 2026 report and
presentation.

CET today, broadcasted live via this

title: Moreld ASA: Ocean Installer receives significant commitment for expanded scope on existing project
AKVA group ASA: Q3 2026 financial reporting
body:
Stable performance and improved profitability
AKVA group ("AKVA") delivered quarterly revenue in Q3 2026 of NOK 959 million, a
decrease of 14% compared to Q3 2025.
High quarterly EBITDA of NOK 170 million, an increase of NOK 22 million or 15%
compared to Q3 2025.
Order intake of NOK 714 million in the quarter and solid order backlog of NOK
2,718 million at the end of Q3 2026.
A dividend of NOK 1 per share was on September 22 for the second half year.
The strategic review was concluded in October, resulting in a transaction
agreement with Yanmar for a recommended voluntary cash offer of NOK 161 per
share for all shares in AKVA. The transaction is expected to be completed in Q4
2026 subject to fulfilment of regulatory requirements.Transaction-related costs
associated with the transaction will be recognized as an expense in Q4 2026.
The activity level in the third quarter of 2026 was acceptable with revenue of
NOK 959 million and order intake of NOK 714 million.
The order backlog of NOK 2,718 million at the end of Q3 2026 is healthy and
provides a solid foundation for continued organic growth into 2027.
Profitability improved in the third quarter compared to last year, and EBIT
ended at NOK 99 million compared to NOK 89 million last year.
Sea Based (SB)
SB revenue for Q3 2026 ended at NOK 666 million (NOK 770 million). EBITDA and
EBIT for the segment in Q3 ended at NOK 137 million (NOK 113 million) and NOK
83 million (NOK 70 million), respectively. The related EBITDA and EBIT margins
were 20.5% (14.7%) and 12.5% (9.1%).
Order intake in Q3 2026 was NOK 549 million compared to NOK 620 million in Q3
2025. Order backlog ended at NOK 1,315 million compared to NOK 745 million last
year.
The Nordic region experienced a decrease in revenue from NOK 545 million in Q3
2025 to NOK 449 million in Q3 2026.
In the Americas region, the revenue was NOK 130 million, which is a decrease
from NOK 134 million in the third quarter last year.
Europe and Middle East (EME) had a revenue of NOK 87 million in Q3 2026,
compared to NOK 91 million in the third quarter last year.
Land Based (LB)
Revenue for the third quarter was NOK 251 million (NOK 308 million). EBITDA and
EBIT ended at NOK 18 million (NOK 22 million) and NOK 14 million (NOK 19
million), respectively. The related EBITDA and EBIT margins were 7.2% (7.3%) and
5.6% (6.1%).
Order intake in Q3 2026 of NOK 131 million compared to NOK 138 million in Q3
2025. Order backlog ended at NOK 1,191 million compared to NOK 1,435 million
last year.
Digital (DI)
The revenue in the segment was NOK 42 million (NOK 34 million) in Q3 2026.
EBITDA and EBIT ended at NOK 16 million (NOK 12 million) and NOK 2 million (NOK
0 million), respectively. The related EBITDA and EBIT margins were 37.2% (36.0%)
and 3.7% (0.1%).
Order intake in Q3 2026 was NOK 34 million compared to NOK 28 million in Q3
2025. Order backlog ended at NOK 212 million, compared to NOK 183 million last
year.
Balance sheet
Working capital as a percentage of 12 months rolling revenue is 10.7% (10.5%).
Cash and unused credit facilities amounted to NOK 472 million (NOK 442 million)
at the end of Q3. Total assets and total equity amounted to NOK 4,297 million
and NOK 1,407 million respectively, resulting in an equity ratio of 32.8%
(32.4%) at the end of Q3 2026. The leverage ratio was 2.34 as of 31 September
2026 and AKVA was in compliance with all bank covenants.
Dividend
The Company's main objective is to maximize the return on the investment made by
its shareholders through both increased share prices and dividend payments. The
company paid a dividend of NOK 1 per share in April for the first half year of
2026 and a dividend of NOK 1 per share in September for the second half year of
2026.
Order Backlog
The order backlog at the end of Q3 was NOK 2,718 million (NOK 2,363 million).
NOK 1,191 million or 44% of total order backlog at the end of Q3 relates to Land
Based.
Outlook
AKVA is foreseeing a continued strong momentum for deep farming concepts.
The company is aiming for revenue of minimum NOK 5 billion and EBIT of 9% in
2027.
AKVA's strategic priorities remain unchanged pending completion of the
transaction with Yanmar, and the company continues to operate its business as
usual.
About AKVA group
AKVA group is a technology and service partner to the aquaculture industry
worldwide. The company has 1 598 employees, offices in 11 countries and had a
total turnover of NOK 4.4 billion in 2025. We are a public listed company
operating in one of the world's fastest growing industries and supply everything
from single components to complete installations, both for sea farming and land
based aquaculture. AKVA group is recognized as a pioneer and technology leader
through more than 40 years.

Mulig tilbakekjøp av egne egenkapitalbevis ifm. spareprogram for ansatte
category: ACQUISITION OR DISPOSAL OF AN ISSUER'S OWN SHARES
body:
SpareBank 1 Østfold Akershus har engasjert SB 1 Markets AS for å undersøke muligheten for tilbakekjøp av inntil 5 600 egenkapitalbevis i banken til bruk i bankens spareprogram for ansatte. Egenkapitalbevisene skal viderefordeles til bankens ansatte i overensstemmelse med bankens spareprogram. Tilbakekjøpet vil bli gjennomført som en omvendt bookbuilding. Banken eier i dag 249 egne egenkapitalbevis. 
Akseptperioden starter omgående med forventet avslutning 13. november kl. 16:30. Akseptperioden kan bli stengt på et tidligere tidspunkt. Banken og tilrettelegger forbeholder seg retten til å utvide akseptperioden og å akseptere ordre mottatt etter avslutning av akseptperioden. 
Endelig kjøpspris per egenkapitalbevis vil bli fastsatt basert på mottatte salgsordre som, etter bankens vurdering, representerer en tilfredsstillende pris og transaksjonsvolum. Den endelige kjøpsprisen vil være identisk for alle selgende egenkapitalbeviseiere. Banken forbeholder seg retten til å redusere antall egenkapitalbevis som kjøpes, alternativt til ikke å kjøpe noen egenkapitalbevis. 
Dersom det samlede antallet egenkapitalbevis som tilbys for salg til den endelige kjøpsprisen overstiger det antall egenkapitalbevis som banken beslutter å erverve, vil avkorting bli foretatt.
Allokering vil i så stor utstrekning som mulig bli gjort på pro rata basis basert på det tilbudte volumet fra hver selgende egenkapitalbeviseier. Formålet er å likebehandle alle egenkapitalbeviseiere basert på deres indikerte interesse i tilbudet på den endelige kjøpsprisen. 
Mottatte salgsordre er bindende og ugjenkallelige og kan ikke trekkes tilbake, kanselleres eller endres av den selgende egenkapitalbeviseieren etter at den har blitt mottatt av tilrettelegger. Den selgende egenkapitalbeviseieren plikter å selge de tilbudte egenkapitalbevisene til banken til de tilbudte vilkårene hvis og på det tidspunkt tilbudet er akseptert av banken, uavhengig av om banken beslutter å kjøpe et lavere antall egenkapitalbevis fra den selgende egenkapitalbeviseieren enn den respektive egenkapitalbeviseieren hadde tilbudt for salg. 
Dersom transaksjonen gjennomføres, vil prissetting følge omgående etter utløp av akseptperioden. Basert på det ovenfor angitte tidspunktet for avslutning av akseptperioden, forventes allokering utført 13. november 2026 (T), og oppgjør er forventet på eller rundt 17. november 2026 (T+2) gjennom en levering mot betaling (DVP)-transaksjon. Hvis akseptperioden forlenges, vil disse datoene justeres tilsvarende. 
Tilbakekjøpet er basert på fullmakt fra bankens ordinære representantskapsmøte den 26. mars 2025. 
Egenkapitalbeviseiere som har spørsmål om transaksjonen og ønsker å selge egenkapitalbevis, bes kontakte Joakim Hafsmo i SB 1 Markets AS på: Dir. tlf.: +47 24147468 Mob.: 47 99224346 e-post: joakim.hafsmo@sb1markets.no

title: Sentia awarded phase 2 of NRK s new headquarters at Normannsløkka
body:
HENT, a subsidiary of Sentia, has today signed a contract with the Norwegian
Broadcasting Corporation (NRK) for phase 2 of NRK's new headquarters at
Normannsløkka, Ensjø, in Oslo. The contract value is approximately NOK 2.800
million, excluding VAT.
The contract is a design-and-build contract based on collaboration (samspill).
HENT and NRK have worked together in phase 1 since April 2025 which is now
completed. The project now moves into the construction phase, with completion
planned for Desember 2029.
The building will have a floor area of 53500 square metres and will include
studios, production facilities, offices and public areas. The site is located
close to railway and metro lines, which places particular demands on the
execution of the project. The project is a candidate to become a FutureBuilt
pilot project, a programme for climate-friendly buildings with high
architectural quality. This involves stricter requirements for reduced
greenhouse gas emissions than for conventional buildings.
-Over the past 18 months, we have developed the project through open
collaboration with NRK and our partners. This provides a solid foundation for
delivering a technically demanding project. NRK is one of Norway's most
important public institutions, and the new headquarters will be a building
open to the public and a boost for Ensjø and eastern Oslo. It is a building we
are proud to construct, says Jan Jahren, CEO of Sentia.

title: Sentia tildelt fase 2 for NRKs nye hovedkontor på Normannsløkka
body:
HENT, et datterselskap av Sentia, har i dag inngått kontrakt med NRK om fase 2
for NRKs nye hovedkontor på Normannsløkka på Ensjø i Oslo. Kontraktsverdien er
ca. 2.800 millioner kroner ekskl. mva.
Kontrakten er en totalentreprise i samspill. HENT og NRK har siden april 2025
samarbeidet i fase 1, som nå er avsluttet. Prosjektet går over i byggefasen,
med planlagt ferdigstillelse i desember 2029.
Bygget får et areal på 53500 kvm og omfatter blant annet studioer,
produksjonsarealer, konsertstudio, kontorer og publikumsarealer. Tomten ligger
tett på jernbane og t-bane, noe som stiller særlige krav til gjennomføringen.
Prosjektet er en kandidat til å bli et forbildeprosjekt i FutureBuilt, et
program for klimavennlige bygg med høy arkitektonisk kvalitet. Det innebærer
strengere krav til reduserte klimagassutslipp enn for vanlige bygg.
-Gjennom 1,5 år har vi utviklet prosjektet i et åpent samspill med NRK og våre
samarbeidspartnere. Det gir et godt grunnlag for å gjennomføre et teknisk
krevende prosjekt. NRK er en av Norges viktigste samfunnsinstitusjoner, og det
nye hovedkontoret blir et åpent bygg for publikum og et løft for Ensjø og Oslo
øst. Det er et bygg vi er stolte av å få bygge, sier Jan Jahren, konsernsjef i
Sentia.

title: Hunter Group ASA - Business Update on reduced charter hire from one of the counterparties.
body:

Reference is made to the stock announcements published by Hunter Group ASA (the
"Company") on 15 April 2026 and 18 May 2026 and 9 June 2026 and 21 July 2026 and
10 August 2026 and 8 September 2026 and 9 October 2026 regarding one of the
Company's long-term contractual counterparty's reduced payments of time charter
hire in March, April, May, June, July, August and September.

approximately USD 18,620,000 less than the amount due for October 2026.

continued breach of contract and will continue to take all necessary steps to
protect its contractual rights.

SOUTH AFRICA AND SOUTH KOREA, OR ANY OTHER JURISDICTION IN WHICH THE RELEASE,
PUBLICATION OR DISTRIBUTION WOULD BE UNLAWFUL.
Reference is made to the recommended voluntary cash offer to acquire all issued
and outstanding shares in AKVA group ASA (the "Company" or "AKVA") by Pontos
Bidco AS (the "Offeror"), a Norwegian private limited liability company
indirectly owned by Yanmar Holdings Co., Ltd. ("Yanmar"), at NOK 161 per share
on the terms and conditions set out in the offer document dated 6 November 2026
(the "Offer Document") (the "Offer"). Reference is also made to the stock
exchange announcement published on 6 November 2026 regarding commencement of the
period where shareholders of the Company may accept the Offer (the "Offer
Period") subject to the terms and conditions in the Offer Document.
The board of directors of the Company has unanimously recommended that all
shareholders accept the Offer and PricewaterhouseCoopers AS has provided an
independent expert statement in accordance with section 6-16 of the Norwegian
Securities Trading Act, which states that the Offer is fair from a financial
point of view. The independent expert statement is appended to an announcement
from the Company dated 6 November 2026.
At the time of this announcement, and subject to customary verifications of
acceptances received, the Offeror has received acceptances from shareholders of
the Company under the Offer for 33,584,769 shares representing approximately
92.06% of the issued and outstanding share capital and voting rights of the
Company. Subject to customary verifications of acceptances received, this means
that the "Minimum Acceptance" closing condition as set out in Section 1.4
("Closing Conditions") of the Offer Document has been satisfied. Completion of
the Offer remains subject to the satisfaction or waiver of the other closing
conditions set out in Section 1.4 ("Closing Conditions") of the Offer Document,
including the closing condition "Regulatory Approvals", and such conditions
remaining satisfied until settlement of the Offer. As at the date of this
announcement, clearance from the Norwegian Competition Authority and foreign
direct investment clearance in the United Kingdom remain pending. The Offeror
will publish a separate announcement once all regulatory approvals have been
obtained.
The Offer Period expires on 20 November 2026 at 16:30 CET.
As set out in Section 2.15 ("Compulsory Acquisition of Shares") of the Offer
Document, subject to and following completion of the Offer and the Offeror
having become the owner of more than 90% of the total issued shares and voting
rights in the Company, the Offeror intends to carry out a compulsory acquisition
of the remaining shares of the Company in accordance with Section 4-25 of the
Norwegian Public Limited Liability Companies Act. Further, subject to and
following completion of the Offer, the Offeror also intends to take steps to
delist the Company's shares from Euronext Oslo Børs as further described in
Section 2.16 ("Delisting of the Shares") of the Offer Document.
Shareholders who want to accept the Offer must, prior to expiry of the Offer
Period on 20 November 2026 at 16:30 CET and in accordance with the procedures
set out in the Offer Document, duly complete and return the acceptance form
which is included in the Offer Document. Subject to regulatory restrictions in
certain jurisdictions, the Offer Document is available at the following webpage:
https://www.arctic.com/offerings
Shareholders who own shares registered in the name of brokers, banks, investment
companies or other nominees, must contact such persons to accept the Offer. The
Offer may only be accepted on the basis of the Offer Document. The complete
terms and conditions of the Offer are set out in the Offer Document.

Arctic Securities AS is acting as financial advisor for the Offeror.

With reference to the authorization given by the Annual General Meeting of Wilh. Wilhelmsen Holding ASA (the "Company") on 30 April 2026 for the Board of Directors to acquire up to 10% of outstanding shares in the Company, the Company hereby launches a tender offer to purchase up to 220,000 shares in the Company (the "Offering"). The Offering will be conducted as a reverse book building process in which shareholders can submit sales offers.
The acquisition of A-shares and B-shares, and the split between the two share classes, are subject to offer demand and prices and as further determined by the Company's board. The Company reserves the right, at its own discretion, to acquire fewer shares or no shares at all in the Offering. 
The purchase of shares will not impact previously announced dividend guidance. The purpose of the Offering is to cancel the shares acquired in the Offering or settlement of shares in the employee share program.
The Company has mandated Clarksons Securities AS as sole bookrunner. 
All shareholders in the Company are invited to sell shares in the Offering, subject to the restrictions set out herein. Shareholders wanting to sell shares in the Offering are required to complete and send the attached acceptance form to Clarksons Securities AS at subscription.oslo@clarksons.com before the end of the Application Period (as defined below). Existing customers of Clarksons Securities AS can contact their respective Sales Representative at Clarksons Securities AS, or call +47 22 01 63 00, with their respective volume and price targets. 
The Offering will be carried out by means of a reverse book building process where the Company, through Clarksons Securities AS, will receive offers for desired volume(s) at desired price(s) for sale from the shareholders. The Company reserves the right to, at its own discretion, accept any volume up to an accepted price, or to reject all received offers in the contemplated Offering. The Company may further, at its sole discretion amend, terminate or withdraw the Offering at any time until the time of completion of the Offering.
The application period for tendering shares in the Offering commences at 09:00 (CET) on 9 November 2026 and is expected to close at 16:30 (CET) on 10 November 2026 (the "Application Period"). The final price offered by the Company and the allocation of tendered shares are expected to be resolved by the Company on or about 10 November 2026, the trade date is expected to be on or about 11 November 2026 and the settlement date is expected to be on or about 13 November 2026. The settlement will either be conducted on a normal delivery-versus-payment basis (DVP) or through the VPS system. The Company reserves the right to extend the Application Period at its own discretion. If the Application Period is extended the other dates referred to herein may be amended accordingly.
The Company will - in the event of receiving acceptances above 220,000 shares - depending on the prices and volumes shown by selling shareholders and subject to the restrictions set out herein and applicable legislation, allocate shares at its discretion between the share classes, with the equal treatment of shareholders as the primary objective.
The Company currently has a total of 42,350,000 shares issued, of which the Company holds 663,078 A-shares and 190,025 B-shares prior to the Offering,

title: Cadeler plc publishes a notice of compulsory acquisition of the shares in Cadeler A/S held by remaining minority shareholders
category: ADDITIONAL REGULATED INFORMATION REQUIRED TO BE DISCLOSED UNDER THE LAWS OF A MEMBER STATE
body:
9 November 2026 - Cadeler plc hereby announces that it has decided to exercise its rights under sections 70 and 72 of the Danish Companies Act to initiate and complete a compulsory acquisition of the shares in Cadeler A/S held by remaining minority shareholders (the "Compulsory Acquisition") in connection with the redomiciliation of the Cadeler group's parent company from Denmark to the United Kingdom (the "Redomiciliation").
Reference is made to the stock exchange announcements published by Cadeler A/S on 21 September 2026, 2 November 2026 and 5 November 2026 regarding the voluntary share exchange offer made by Cadeler plc to all holders of shares (including shares represented by American Depositary Shares (ADSs), each representing four (4) shares in Cadeler A/S) in Cadeler A/S to exchange each share in Cadeler A/S for one (1) share in Cadeler plc, each with a nominal value of USD 1.00 (the "Offer") and the section titled "Squeeze-out", in which Cadeler plc informed the shareholders of Cadeler A/S about the contemplated compulsory acquisition following completion of the Offer.
Cadeler plc holds shares representing more than 90 per cent of the total number and of the aggregate voting power of the outstanding shares in Cadeler A/S following settlement of the Offer. On this basis, Cadeler plc is entitled to, and has resolved to, exercise its right to complete the Compulsory Acquisition of the shares held by the remaining minority shareholders of Cadeler A/S in accordance with sections 70 and 72 of the Danish Companies Act.
Accordingly, all remaining minority shareholders of Cadeler A/S are pursuant to the attached statutory notice for the Compulsory Acquisition (the "Statutory Notice") formally requested by Cadeler plc to transfer their shares in Cadeler A/S to Cadeler plc within a period of four (4) weeks expiring on 7 December 2026 at 23:59 (CET) (the "Compulsory Acquisition Period") at a price of NOK 58.42 per share in Cadeler A/S of a nominal value of DKK 1.00, as determined by Cadeler plc in accordance with the Danish Companies Act, being the volume-weighted average price (VWAP) of the Cadeler A/S shares on the Oslo Stock Exchange (OSE) over the 30 trading days immediately preceding the initiation of the Offer (the "Redemption Price"), subject to the terms and conditions of the Statutory Notice.
Shareholders in Cadeler A/S are informed that, after expiry of the Compulsory Acquisition Period, Cadeler plc will, against payment of the aggregate Redemption Price, compulsorily acquire the shares in Cadeler A/S held by the minority shareholders who have not voluntarily transferred their shares to Cadeler plc prior to the expiry of the Compulsory Acquisition Period, and consequently become the sole holder of all issued and outstanding shares in Cadeler A/S.
The Statutory Notice will be published in the IT systems of the Danish Business Authority, distributed to the shareholders of Cadeler A/S who have elected to receive electronic notices of general meetings through the share registry, and made available on the website of Cadeler A/S with an acceptance form.
With reference to the stock exchange announcements made by Cadeler A/S on 5 November 2026, shareholders of Cadeler A/S are also reminded that the Oslo Stock Exchange and the New York Stock Exchange have suspended trading of the shares (and, as applicable, the shares represented by American Depositary Shares) of Cadeler A/S with effect from 5 November 2026.
DNB Carnegie, part of DNB Bank ASA, is acting as settlement agent in connection with the Compulsory Acquisition and Computershare Inc. is acting as exchange agent and Georgeson LLC is acting as information agent in the United States to Cadeler ADS holders.

Cadeler plc (Cadeler) is a global leader in offshore wind turbine transport and installation. The company owns and operates the industry's largest fleet of jack-up offshore wind installation vessels and is expanding its capabilities into full-scope foundation transport and installation, as well as operations & maintenance. With its modern fleet and depth of expertise across onshore and offshore operations, Cadeler supports the safe, efficient and reliable delivery of offshore wind projects worldwide. Cadeler is listed on both the New York Stock Exchange and the Oslo Stock Exchange, under the ticker "CDLR". For more information, please visit www.cadeler.com.

DNB Bank ASA - status of share buy-back programme after week 45 2026
category: ACQUISITION OR DISPOSAL OF AN ISSUER'S OWN SHARES
body:
On 21 October 2026, DNB Bank ASA ("DNB") announced that the company has decided
to initiate a share buy-back programme comprising up to 0.75% of the company's
own shares, which represents a total of 10,804,986 shares.
Up to 7,131,291 shares will be purchased on trading venues by 18 December 2026,
and a proposal to cancel the shares will be submitted to the next Annual General
Meeting. At the same meeting it will also be proposed to redeem the remaining
shares - up to 3,673,695 shares - from the Norwegian Government, represented by
the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Fisheries ("NFD"), so that NFD's ownership
interest of 34% remains unchanged.
The total consideration paid for the shares purchased under the buy-back
programme, including the shares that will be proposed redeemed from NFD, will
not exceed NOK 3,790 million.
During week 45 of 2026, DNB purchased 825,792 own shares at an average price of
NOK 322.2580. Following this, DNB has purchased a total of 2,491,292 own shares
under the current buy-back programme, corresponding to 0.17% of the shares in
the company.
Furthermore, there is a correction to the number of shares repurchased on 29
October. The correct number of shares is 205,000, not 180,000 as previously
reported.

title: Notification of claim received in connection with tender for contract
body:
Haugesund, 9 November 2026 - Reach Subsea AS, a wholly owned subsidiary of Reach Subsea ASA, has been served with a statement of claim from Statnett SF. Statnett claims damages of up to NOK 158.5 million plus interest.
Reach Subsea AS firmly rejects the claim and considers it to be without merit. The claim relates to a Statnett tender for cable installation. Reach Subsea AS submitted a conditional tender and the conditions for the tender were not met and no contract was signed.
Statnett subsequently resumed negotiations with another tenderer and awarded the contract to that tenderer. Statnett claims damages for the price difference between the two tenders. 
Reach Subsea AS will defend its position in the legal proceedings.
-ENDS-
For more information please contact:
Arne Joa
Chief Financial Officer
Reach Subsea ASA
investors@reachsubsea.com
+47 474 51 344
About Reach Subsea
Reach Subsea delivers its services through a versatile fleet of vessels, including survey, IMR, construction support, and remote vessels. Our teams operate worldwide, providing inspection, maintenance, construction support, survey and data services across multiple industries, supporting clients throughout every stage of their project lifecycles. Our offshore teams are powered by advanced ROV technology and backed by onshore engineering expertise, turning complex ocean challenges into reliable solutions. With over 500 skilled professionals and offices in Norway, Sweden, the UK, the US, Brazil, Trinidad, Australia, and Singapore, our vision-'Sustainable access to ocean space'-drives safe, innovative, and sustainable subsea operations.
This information is considered to be inside information pursuant to the EU Market Abuse Regulation (MAR) and is subject to the disclosure requirements pursuant to MAR article 17 and Section 5-12 of the Norwegian Securities Trading Act. title: 2020 Bulkers Ltd. (Euronext Oslo Børs  2020  and Euronext NOTC  2020T )   Execution of new USD 146 million senior facilities agreement
body:
Oslo, 9 November 2026
2020 Bulkers Ltd. (the "Company") announces that its wholly-owned subsidiary
UMAS 50 AS has entered into a USD 146 million senior facilities agreement for
the refinancing of the Company's group of wholly-owned ship-owning companies.
The facilities have been arranged by a syndicate of Norwegian and European
banks.
The agreement comprises a USD 110 million term loan facility for
part-financing vessel acquisitions and refinancing existing vessel
indebtedness (including seller credits), a USD 10 million revolving credit
facility for general corporate and working capital purposes, and a USD 26
million revolving facility for the purpose of financing special periodical
surveys.
The facilities bear interest at compounded SOFR plus a margin of 3.35% per
annum and mature on 30 October 2030. The term facility is repayable in
quarterly instalments of approximately 4% of each tranche's original principal
amount, commencing six months after the relevant drawdown, with a balloon
payment of 40% payable at maturity in addition to the final ordinary
instalment. The revolving SPS facility is subject to a scheduled maximum
outstanding amount that varies over the life of the facility. The facilities
agreement otherwise contains financial covenants customary for this type of
financing, including customary covenants in relation to dividends and
distributions.
Completion of the refinancing and drawdown under the facilities remain subject
to customary conditions precedent.

title: Lerøy Seafood Group ASA: Third quarter 2026 results
body:
LERØY SEAFOOD GROUP ASA: STRONG EARNINGS IMPROVEMENT, GOOD BIOLOGICAL
DEVELOPMENT AND STRONG CASH FLOW
"Operational EBIT in the third quarter of 2026 was NOK 459 million, compared
with NOK 15 million in the same quarter last year. The improvement reflects good
biological development and lower costs in Farming, as well as a strong quarter
in Market Operations. At the same time, we are delivering strong cash flow, and
net interest-bearing debt was reduced by NOK 676 million during the quarter,"
says CEO Henning Beltestad.
FARMING: GOOD BIOLOGICAL DEVELOPMENT AND LOWER COSTS
Operational EBIT in Farming was NOK 113 million in the third quarter of 2026,
compared with NOK -306 million in the same period last year. Harvest volume of
salmon and trout was 54,680 GWT, eight percent lower than the year before.
"We continue to see good biological development, and all three of our Norwegian
farming regions delivered improved results compared with the same quarter last
year. Cost levels have declined, while we have also built high standing biomass,
providing a good basis for the coming quarters," says Henning Beltestad.
Harvest volume guidance for Norway is maintained at 195,000 GWT for 2026, with
the same volume expected in 2027. Including the Group's share of Scottish Sea
Farms, total harvest volume is expected to be approximately 215,000 GWT in 2026
and approximately 217,500 GWT in 2027.
MARKET OPERATIONS: STRONG QUARTER
Market Operations delivered Operational EBIT of NOK 446 million in the third
quarter of 2026, compared with NOK 410 million in the same period last year. The
EBIT margin was 5.4 percent, up from 4.9 percent in the third quarter of 2025.
The improvement was mainly driven by higher earnings in primary processing.
"Market Operations delivered a strong quarter. This development is in line with
our previously communicated expectation of significantly improved earnings in
the second half of the year," says Henning Beltestad.
WILD CATCH: LOWER EXPECTATIONS FOR 2026
Operational EBIT in Wild Catch was NOK -20 million in the third quarter of
2026, compared with NOK 3 million in the same period last year. Catch volume
declined by 24 percent to 10,216 tonnes. Higher prices did not fully offset
lower catch volume and higher bunker fuel prices.
"Prices for saithe, cod and haddock have been weaker than previously assumed,
while bunker fuel costs have increased. Against this background, we are reducing
our expectation for Operational EBIT in Wild Catch in 2026 to NOK 315-350
million, compared with the previous expectation of NOK 400-450 million," says
Henning Beltestad.
STRONG CASH FLOW AND PROGRESS IN THE COST PROGRAMME
Cash flow from operating activities was NOK 1,183 million in the third quarter
of 2026, compared with NOK 1,078 million in the same period last year. Net
interest-bearing debt was reduced by NOK 676 million during the quarter to NOK
7,732 million. The equity ratio was 46.4 percent at the end of the quarter.
At the end of the third quarter, NOK 701 million of the Group's NOK 1 billion
cost programme had been realised, while measures representing a further NOK 262
million had been identified and were under implementation.
OUTLOOK
Lerøy enters the fourth quarter with high standing biomass and continued good
biological development. Following several quarters of strong growth, the global
supply of salmon and trout is expected to increase at a slower pace, while
demand remains strong. This points to a more favourable price environment.
The cost programme is progressing according to plan and is expected to reduce
the impact of higher feed prices in 2027.
"We enter the fourth quarter with good biological status, high standing biomass,
a lower cost level and a stronger financial position. At the same time, we
continue to see strong demand for salmon and lower global supply growth.
Together with further effects from the cost programme, this provides a solid
foundation for further development," concludes Henning Beltestad.
This information is subject to the disclosure requirements pursuant to Section
5-12 of the Norwegian Securities Trading Act.

title: Lerøy Seafood Group ASA: Resultat tredje kvartal 2026
body:
LERØY SEAFOOD GROUP ASA: STERK RESULTATFORBEDRING, GOD BIOLOGISK UTVIKLING OG
STERK KONTANTSTRØM
"Operasjonelt driftsresultat i tredje kvartal 2026 ble NOK 459 millioner, mot
NOK 15 millioner i samme kvartal i fjor. Resultatforbedringen reflekterer god
biologisk utvikling og lavere kostnader i Havbruk, samt et sterkt kvartal i
Market Operations. Samtidig leverer vi en sterk kontantstrøm, og netto
rentebærende gjeld er redusert med NOK 676 millioner i kvartalet," sier
konsernsjef Henning Beltestad.
HAVBRUK: GOD BIOLOGISK UTVIKLING OG LAVERE KOSTNADER
Operasjonelt driftsresultat i Havbruk ble NOK 113 millioner i tredje kvartal
2026, mot NOK -306 millioner i samme periode i fjor. Slaktevolumet av laks og
ørret var 54 680 GWT, åtte prosent lavere enn året før.
"Vi har fortsatt god biologisk utvikling, og alle våre tre norske
havbruksregioner leverer resultatforbedring sammenlignet med samme kvartal i
fjor. Kostnadsnivået er redusert, og vi har samtidig bygget en høy stående
biomasse som gir et godt utgangspunkt for kommende kvartaler," sier Henning
Beltestad.
Guidet slaktevolum i Norge opprettholdes på 195 000 GWT i 2026. For 2027
forventes et slaktevolum i Norge på 195 000 GWT. Inkludert konsernets andel av
Scottish Sea Farms forventes samlet slaktevolum på om lag 215 000 GWT i 2026 og
om lag 217 500 GWT i 2027.
MARKET OPERATIONS: STERKT KVARTAL
Market Operations leverte et operasjonelt driftsresultat på NOK 446 millioner i
tredje kvartal 2026, mot NOK 410 millioner i samme periode i fjor. EBIT-marginen
ble 5,4 prosent, opp fra 4,9 prosent i tredje kvartal 2025. Resultatforbedringen
var hovedsakelig drevet av høyere inntjening innen primærprosessering.
"Market Operations leverer et sterkt kvartal. Utviklingen er i tråd med
forventningene som vi kommuniserte etter andre kvartal om vesentlig bedre
inntjening i andre halvår," sier Henning Beltestad.
VILLFANGST: LAVERE FORVENTNINGER TIL 2026
Operasjonelt driftsresultat i Villfangst ble NOK -20 millioner i tredje kvartal
2026, mot NOK 3 millioner i samme periode i fjor. Fangstvolumet ble redusert med
24 prosent til 10 216 tonn. Høyere priser kompenserte ikke fullt ut for lavere
fangstvolum og høyere bunkerspriser.
"Prisene på sei, torsk og hyse har utviklet seg svakere enn vi tidligere la til
grunn, og kostnad til bunkers er økt. På bakgrunn av dette reduserer vi
forventningen til operasjonelt driftsresultat i Villfangst i 2026 til NOK
315-350 millioner, fra tidligere NOK 400-450 millioner," sier Henning Beltestad.
STERK KONTANTSTRØM OG FREMDRIFT I KOSTNADSPROGRAMMET
Kontantstrøm fra operasjonelle aktiviteter ble NOK 1 183 millioner i tredje
kvartal 2026, mot NOK 1 078 millioner i samme periode i fjor. Netto rentebærende
gjeld ble redusert med NOK 676 millioner gjennom kvartalet til NOK 7 732
millioner. Egenkapitalandelen var 46,4 prosent ved utgangen av kvartalet.
Ved utgangen av tredje kvartal er NOK 701 millioner av konsernets
kostnadsprogram på NOK 1 milliard realisert, mens tiltak for ytterligere NOK
262 millioner er identifisert og under gjennomføring.
UTSIKTER
Lerøy går inn i fjerde kvartal med høy stående biomasse og fortsatt god
biologisk utvikling. Etter flere kvartaler med sterk tilbudsvekst forventes
veksten i globalt tilbud av laks og ørret å avta, samtidig som etterspørselen er
sterk. Dette peker mot et marked med et styrket prisbilde.
Kostnadsprogrammet utvikler seg i tråd med planen og ventes å redusere effekten
av høyere fôrpriser i 2027.
"Vi går inn i fjerde kvartal med god biologisk status, høy stående biomasse, et
lavere kostnadsnivå og en sterkere finansiell posisjon. Samtidig ser vi fortsatt
sterk etterspørsel etter laks og lavere global tilbudsvekst. Sammen med videre
effekter fra kostnadsprogrammet gir dette et godt utgangspunkt for den videre
utviklingen," avslutter Henning Beltestad.
Denne opplysningen er informasjonspliktig etter verdipapirhandelloven § 5-12.

title: Financial report Q3 2026
body:
The Group reported operating revenue, including other income, gains and losses, of MNOK 9,228 in Q3 2026, down from MNOK 10,037 in Q3 2025. Adjusted EBITDA was MNOK 1,131 in the quarter, against MNOK 651 in the same period last year. Adjusted EBIT was MNOK 546 in the quarter (Q3 2025: MNOK 78). The increase in earnings is primarily attributable to lower operating costs and improved price realisation in the farming segment. In Peru, the first fishing season had been suspended since late April and was formally closed in August due to warm seawater temperatures and a high proportion of juvenile fish. Austral caught 20% of its quota in the first season, which significantly impacted Austral's revenue and earnings in the quarter. Headwinds in Peru were largely offset by FoodCorp's best third quarter to date. FoodCorp had a third quarter with high activity after very low activity in second quarter, and the catch volume in the quarter was more than doubled compared to last year. This combined with high prices on all finished products contributed to the best third quarter to date.
Scottish Sea Farms Ltd (Norskott Havbruk AS) and Pelagia are the Group's two largest joint ventures. Income from associates before fair value adjustment related to biological assets in the quarter totalled MNOK 83 (Q3 2025: MNOK 4). The equivalent figure including fair value adjustment of biological assets was MNOK 230 (Q3 2025: MNOK -6). Scottish Sea Farms harvested 12,983 GWT this quarter, up 79% from the same period last year. The result in the period was negatively impacted by incident-based mortality. Sites with biological challenges in Q3 were harvested out in October. Please refer to Note 5 in this report and the Q3 2026 presentation.
Income from Pelagia improved compared with Q3 2025. Markets for fishmeal and fish oil (FEED) were generally favourable with a high price level. In consumer products (FOOD), strong competition with FEED and low volumes resulted in high raw material prices. Pelagia's share of net profit was MNOK 78 in the quarter (Q3 2025: MNOK 0). Further information is available under the operational review of segments section in this report and in the Q3 2026 presentation. 
Adjusted EBIT including income from associates was MNOK 629 in the quarter, against MNOK 82 in the same period last year.
Operating profit after fair value adjustment of biological assets and other income and expenses totalled MNOK 876 in the quarter (Q3 2025: MNOK 954). Fair value adjustment related to biological assets in the consolidated Group was MNOK 155, compared with MNOK 947 in Q3 2025. Fair value adjustment related to biological assets recognised in income from associates was MNOK 147, compared with MNOK -10 in Q3 2025.
The Group's net interest expense was MNOK 159 (Q3 2025: MNOK 180). Net other financial items totalled MNOK -40. The equivalent figure in Q3 2025 was MNOK 2.
Profit before tax was MNOK 677 in the quarter (Q3 2025: MNOK 776), and profit after tax in Q3 2026 was MNOK 677, against MNOK 529 in Q3 2025. The change is primarily driven by lower tax expenses and higher profitability in the farming segment. In addition, also higher income from associated companies mainly driven by improved earnings in Pelagia and a positive fair value adjustment of biomass in Scottish Sea Farms Ltd. (Norskott Havbruk AS).
For further information please see attached report and presentation.
Questions and comments may be addressed to the company's CEO, Arne Møgster, or to CFO, Britt Kathrine Drivenes.
This information is subject of the disclosure requirements acc. to Section 5-12 vphl (Norwegian Securities Trading Act).

title: Panoro Energy - Material Helium and Natural Gas Potential Confirmed at ER 376 Onshore South Africa
body:
Oslo, 10 November 2026 - Panoro Energy ASA ("Panoro" or the "Company") is
pleased to announce that following an independent assessment by Sproule ERCE,
material prospective helium and natural gas resource potential has been
confirmed at Exploration Right 376 ("ER 376") onshore South Africa in which
Panoro holds a 100 per cent interest.
Three independent plays have been evaluated for prospective resources:
 - Combined helium and methane gas play in Fractured Basement Precambrian
metasediments of the Ventersdorp and Witwatersrand Groups
 - Regional methane gas play in the Permian Vryheid Sandstones formation
 - Permian Ecca Group coalbed methane play
Results of the independently certified resource evaluation are outlined below,
with ER376 estimated to hold a gross recoverable un-risked mean of 85 Bcf of
helium and over 4 Tcf of Methane.
Eric d'Argentre, Chief Operating Officer and President of Panoro, commented:
"The independent confirmation of material prospective helium and natural gas
resources at ER 376 is an important milestone and underscores the strategic
value and externally overlooked upside we see in the asset. Helium is a future
-facing commodity, with critical applications across advanced industries and a
low-visibility but irreplaceable input to global supply chains. In parallel, the
substantial natural gas potential identified at ER 376 positions the asset
within a compelling domestic market context in South Africa, where new gas
supply can support energy security and help reduce reliance on coal. Having
secured this opportunity through ground-floor entry and advanced it through
robust technical work, we are excited by the high potential now independently
validated by Sproule ERCE and will evaluate the optimal pathway to realise value
for shareholders."
Gross Recoverable Prospective Helium Resources (Bcf)

|Play |1U |2U |3U |Unrisked Mean|CoS (%)|Risked Mean|

Background
Panoro's activity at ER 376 extends back to 2022 when it was initially awarded a
Technical Cooperation Permit (TCP 218). This one-year permit allowed for desktop
geological and geophysical studies to evaluate the potential for a helium and
natural gas plays. Utilising an extensive borehole database, combined with
airborne geophysics, and regional data, Panoro developed a geological
understanding and successfully identified key elements in relation to the helium
and natural gas plays. As a result of this, Panoro opted to convert TCP 218 into
an exploration right, ER 376.
High Potential Helium Basin
Some of the highest global concentrations of helium have been recorded in gas
wells and boreholes in the North Karoo Basin. Helium concentrations of two to
four per cent are common with concentrations in excess of 20 per cent recorded.
While a by-product of natural gas production, Panoro believes that the helium
potential of ER 376 offers a highly attractive outright commercial opportunity
that can be both scalable and de-linked from hydrocarbon prices. Numerous
strategic industries including the global semiconductor, fibre optic, medical
imaging and aerospace industries are irreversibly dependent on a stable and
secure supply of Helium. With the US strategic Helium reserve depleting in
recent years and conflict in the Middle East severely affecting helium supply,
the need for less dominant alternative reliable supply from geopolitically low
risk sources is intensifying. Panoro believes that South Africa has the
potential to become a strategically important source of helium supply to the
global market.
Natural Gas Opportunity
The primary proven play concept Panoro at ER 376 is biogenic gas generated by
groundwater circulating through large faults and contacting bacteria, meaning
the natural gas is generated through a continual process and therefore is
renewable.
Panoro believes that favourable dynamics exist for domestic gas opportunities in
South Africa where power demand is not always met. South Africa has removed the
generation licensing threshold, allowing qualifying private power generation
projects of any capacity to proceed without a generation licence, subject to
applicable regulatory requirements. In the event that commercial quantities of
natural gas are proved on ER 376 its close proximity to some of South Africa's
major demand centres lends itself as a potential supply source for domestic gas
to power projects. South Africa presently has a high dependency on coal which
accounts for approximately 70 per cent of energy by source in the country. Any
new gas supply to underpin domestic power generation projects can therefore help
displace coal as the dominant energy source.

title: High activity and solid operations in the third quarter
body:
Sentia ASA delivers a solid third quarter of 2026, with good activity, strong
project execution and several new contracts. Revenue increased by 12.9 per
cent compared with the same period last year.
Key figures Q3 2026
- Revenue: NOK 3,217 million (2,850), up 12.9%
- Profit before tax: NOK 191 million (189)
- Order intake: NOK 3,583 million (1,044)
- Order backlog: NOK 18,702 million (19,535)
- Net financial position: NOK 4,146 million (3,252)
-- We are delivering another quarter of high activity and good operations
across the group. Profitability is solid, and a strong order backlog gives us
a good starting point for 2027. At the same time, we know that good project
execution is not only about what we deliver, but how we deliver it. That
places high demands on leadership, collaboration and safety, and that is where
we will continue to stand out, says Jan Jahren, CEO of Sentia.
New projects in the quarter
During the quarter, HENT signed a contract with Nscale to expand the data
centre in the Narvik region with two new buildings totalling 75 MW. HENT will
thereby build three buildings with a combined capacity of 100 MW for Nscale.
HENT also signed an agreement with Calmar Gruppen for the refurbishment and
conversion of Klubbgata 3, located in Stavanger, into a hotel.
Sentia Sverige also started new projects in the quarter, including a new
preschool in Tegelviken in Kvicksund for Eskilstuna Kommunfastighet through
SSEA.

prosjektgjennomføring, samt flere nye kontrakter. Omsetningen økte med 12,9
prosent sammenlignet med samme periode i fjor.

title: Kapitalmarkedsdag: DNB godt posisjonert for videre lønnsom vekst
body:
DNB arrangerer i dag, 10. november 2026, konsernets kapitalmarkedsdag. Her
presenteres strategiske prioriteringer og finansielle mål for perioden
2027-2029.
DNB øker sine ambisjoner med følgende finansielle mål for regnskapsåret 2029:
 - Egenkapitalavkastning (ROE) over 15 prosent
 - Kostnadsgrad (cost/income) under 38 prosent
 - Ren kjernekapitaldekning (CET1) over 16,3 prosent
 - Utbetalingsgrad over 50 prosent, med en ambisjon om å øke nominelt utbytte
per aksje hvert år
Vi tar sikte på å nå målene innen utgangen av 2028. DNBs eksisterende
finansielle mål om en egenkapitalavkastning på over 14 prosent og en
kostnadsgrad under 40 prosent videreføres for regnskapsårene 2027 og 2028, med
gradvis fremgang mot de nye målene i perioden. Målet for ren
kjernekapitaldekning og utbyttepolitikken gjelder uendret gjennom hele perioden.
I tillegg har DNB en ambisjon om å levere 3-4 prosent årlig utlånsvekst over tid
og mer enn 9 prosent årlig vekst i netto provisjons- og gebyrinntekter gjennom
syklusen.
DNB har levert sterke resultater og lønnsom vekst siden forrige
kapitalmarkedsdag i 2024. Med ledende posisjoner i det norske markedet, en
styrket nordisk plattform og sterke posisjoner innen sparing og investering, har
DNB et godt utgangspunkt for videre lønnsom vekst. Banken skal samtidig
fortsette å utvikle kundeløsningene gjennom helhetlig rådgivning og bruk av
teknologi og kunstig intelligens, samt øke kapitallette inntekter fram mot 2029.
- DNB har en sterk posisjon og vi har over tid vist at vi leverer på våre
finansielle mål. Nå skal vi bygge videre på våre ledende posisjoner i Norge,
samtidig som vi utnytter mulighetene en styrket nordisk plattform gir oss. Med
DNB Carnegie har vi fått større bredde og kraft i vårt nordiske tilbud og nye
muligheter til å skape verdi for kundene på tvers av konsernet. Samtidig endrer
teknologi og kunstig intelligens måten vi leverer tjenester på og lar oss bygge
en enda bedre bank for kundene våre, sier konsernsjef Kjerstin Braathen.
Som tidligere kommunisert i børsmeldingen 6. oktober 2026 gjennomfører DNB en
nedbemanning i Technology & Services. Dette medfører restruktureringskostnader
på om lag 225 millioner kroner, som vil bli regnskapsført i fjerde kvartal 2026.
Presentasjonen fra kapitalmarkedsdagen er vedlagt. Arrangementet blir
direktesendt fra kl. 12:00 GMT (kl. 13:00 norsk tid) på www.ir.dnb.no.

title: Capital Markets Day: DNB well positioned for further profitable growth
body:
Today, 10 November 2026, DNB is holding the Group's Capital Markets Day,
presenting strategic priorities and financial targets for the period 2027-2029.
DNB is raising its ambitions with the following financial targets for the
financial year 2029:
 - Return on equity (ROE) above 15 per cent
 - Cost/income ratio below 38 per cent
 - Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) capital ratio above 16.3 per cent
 - Payout ratio above 50 per cent, with an ambition to increase the nominal
dividend per share every year
We aim to deliver on the targets by year-end 2028. DNB's existing financial
targets of a return on equity of more than 14 per cent and a cost/income ratio
below 40 per cent will be continued for the financial years 2027 and 2028, with
gradual progress towards the new targets throughout the period. The targets
relating to the CET1 capital ratio target and dividend policy will remain
unchanged throughout the period.
In addition, DNB has an ambition to deliver annual lending growth of 3-4 per
cent over time and annual growth in net commission and fee income of more than 9
per cent through the cycle.
DNB has delivered strong results and profitable growth since the previous
Capital Markets Day, in 2024. With leading positions in the Norwegian market, a
strengthened Nordic platform and strong positions in savings and investments,
DNB has a good starting point for further profitable growth. At the same time,
the bank will continue to develop its solutions for customers through a wide
range of advisory services and use of technology and artificial intelligence, as
well as by increasing capital-light income leading up to 2029.
"DNB has a strong position, and over time we have proven that we deliver on our
financial targets. Now we will continue to build on our leading positions in
Norway, while also exploring the opportunities provided by a strengthened Nordic
platform. With DNB Carnegie, our Nordic offering has become more wide-ranging
and powerful, and we have new opportunities to create value for our customers
throughout the Group. At the same time, technology and artificial intelligence
are changing the way we deliver services and letting us build an even better
bank for our customers," says Group Chief Executive Officer (CEO) Kjerstin
Braathen.
As previously communicated in the stock exchange announcement on 6 October 2026,
DNB is carrying out workforce reductions in Technology & Services. This will
result in restructuring costs of approximately NOK 225 million, to be recognised
in the fourth quarter of 2026.

streamed from 12:00 GMT (13:00 CET) at www.ir.dnb.no.
