title: Third quarter financial results: Strong operating results across the portfolio
category: ADDITIONAL REGULATED INFORMATION REQUIRED TO BE DISCLOSED UNDER THE LAWS OF A MEMBER STATE
body:
(Arendal, 10 November 2026) Arendals Fossekompani ASA (OSE: AFK) reported revenue of NOK 892 million (853 million) and an operating profit of NOK 104 million (33 million) in the third quarter of 2026. Ordinary profit after tax, but before non-controlling interests, totalled NOK 118 million (141 million).
The 5% increase in Group revenue YoY was driven by high electricity prices and growth in Tekna. Operating margin for the quarter was 12% (4%). The improvement was driven by stronger profitability in ENRX, high electricity prices and reduced exposure to early-phase companies.
"Q3 was marked by strong operational performance across the portfolio. Volue delivered well above the Rule of 40 with 24% revenue growth and a 25% adjusted cash EBITDA margin. ENRX's operational focus continued to pay off, with improved profitability and order intake up 33% YoY. Tekna had a very strong quarter with 61% revenue growth, and our hydropower business delivered an operating profit of NOK 64 million on the back of high power prices," says Benjamin Golding, Chief Executive Officer of Arendals Fossekompani.
Portfolio highlights
Volue: Continued growth while operating leverage coming through
Revenue amounted to EUR 38.7 million (31.3 million), corresponding to YoY growth of 24%. The growth was largely driven by recurring revenue which grew by 25%. A total of 49 new customers were contracted in the quarter. The adjusted cash EBITDA was EUR 9.6 million (7.6 million), corresponding to a margin of 25% (24%). 
ENRX: Profitable growth and commercial momentum
Revenue amounted to EUR 33.3 million (31.2 million), corresponding to YoY growth of 7%. Operating profit improved to EUR 2.8 million (-0.9 million), driven by higher revenue and tight cost control. Order intake was EUR 41 million, up 33% YoY, corresponding to a book-to-bill of 1.2, driven by North America and Asia. Order backlog was EUR 73 million, up 19.5% YoY.
NSSLGlobal: Significant new contracts 
Revenue was GBP 24.5 million (24.9 million) with high airtime traffic offset by project invoicing timing effects. Operating profit was GBP 3.8 million (4.6 million) due to lower gross margins and higher operating costs compared to Q3 2025. During the quarter, NSSLGlobal won contracts with a value of GBP 38.6 million (16.8 million) across the government and maritime sectors. 
Tekna: Profitability and enhanced commercial visibility
Revenue was CAD 13.4 million (8.3 million). The YoY growth of 61% was driven by sustained Materials demand and strong order and project execution in Systems. Adjusted EBITDA was CAD 2.9 million (0.5 million), corresponding to a margin of 21.5% (5.6%). Order intake was CAD 10.6 million (5.3 million), reflecting robust Materials demand across aerospace, defence and medical. Order backlog ended at CAD 25.5 million, up 40% YoY, extending visibility into 2027.
AFK Vannkraft: Strong quarter with high prices
Revenue in Q3 amounted to NOK 90 million (59 million), driven by high electricity prices. Operating profit was NOK 64 million (36 million), corresponding to an operating margin of 71% (60%).
Structural changes in the portfolio 
During the quarter, Arendals Fossekompani closed the previously announced transaction bringing in TA Associates as a new strategic partner in Volue. The transaction, which involved sale of shares, resulted in a gain of NOK 82 million recognised in the consolidated financial statements. After closing, Arendals Fossekompani holds 35.67% of Faraday Topco, the holding company that indirectly owns all shares in Volue. 
In September, NSSLGlobal acquired MetOcean Telematics (UK) Ltd, a provider of security, surveillance and IoT asset tracking solutions. The acquisition broadens NSSLGlobal's product offering and gives access to adjacent markets by combining communications and security capabilities.
As a result of financial restructuring in Veyt, Arendals Fossekompani reduced its ownership in the company from 62.1% to 33.9% in the quarter. Consequently, Veyt's financials are no longer consolidated in the Arendals Fossekompani Group. 
Solid financial position 
The financial position of Arendals Fossekompani Parent company remains solid. The company's available cash on 30 September amounted to NOK 941 million. In addition, the company has undrawn credit facilities of NOK 2,126 million, securing available liquidity of NOK 3,067 million at the end of the quarter.
"Our strong balance sheet gives us the financial flexibility to support our existing portfolio and to capture opportunities as they become actionable," says Golding.
Outlook 
Arendals Fossekompani Group revenue in 2026 is expected to be in line with 2025. Operating profit is expected to be significantly higher in 2026.

title: Atea Share Savings Program- notification of trade
body:
Reference is made to prior stock exchange notices regarding the Employee Share
Savings Program.
Under the terms of the Program, participating employees may allocate a fixed
amount of their monthly after-tax salary to purchase shares in Atea ASA (up to a
maximum per month of NOK 1,000 in Norway, SEK 1,000 in Sweden, DKK 700 in
Denmark and EUR 100 per month in Finland and the Baltic countries). Shares are
purchased by employees from Atea ASA's treasury share holdings at market price.
The price of the shares purchased is determined based on the volume-weighted
average price of the ATEA share on the day preceding the share transfer.
As an additional incentive, participating employees will receive one "bonus"
share for each two ordinary shares purchased under the Program after a vesting
period in which the specified ordinary shares must be held. The vesting period
is three years for executive management and two years for all other employees.
The participant must also remain employed by Atea during the vesting period in
order to receive the bonus share. The unvested "bonus" share is treated as a
restricted stock unit (RSU) under IFRS 2 Share-Based Payment.
On 10 November 2026, Atea ASA transferred 76,381 treasury shares to employees
based on the following transactions in the Employee Share Savings program. After
the transactions, Atea ASA owns 742,520 of its own shares.
1. Employee share purchase
On 10 November 2026, 3,269 employees in the Atea group purchased a total of
52,414 shares in Atea ASA. Shares were purchased from Atea's treasury share
holdings at a share price of NOK 168.55 per share, corresponding to the volume
-weighted average share price on 5 November 2026. The cost of the shares will be
deducted from the employees' after-tax salary in November, December and January.
2. Award of bonus shares
On 10 November 2026, employees received the right to bonus shares after having
held shares purchased through the program for the required vesting period. In
total, 23,967 shares have been transferred from Atea's treasury holdings to
employee accounts.

Akastor ASA: Third Quarter Results 2026
body:
Third Quarter Highlights:
* Dividend of NOK 2.50 per share approved, supported by cash proceeds received
 in October from NES Fircroft and the sale of Skandi Peregrino.
* Total distributions since July 2025 thereby amount to approximately NOK 1.5
 billion, or NOK 5.65 per share.
* HMH delivered adjusted EBITDA of USD 38 million at a 22% margin. Equipment
 order activity was below expectations, with several opportunities shifting
 to later periods, while HMH remains confident in the underlying deepwater
 fundamentals.
* AKOFS Offshore maintained strong operations across the fleet and completed a
 USD 300 million fleet refinancing, securing long-term funding and ownership
 of Aker Wayfarer.
* Post quarter-end, Akastor received a USD 57.4 million cash distribution
 following NES Fircroft's refinancing and subsequent shareholder
 recapitalisation.
* The sale of Skandi Peregrino was completed in October for USD 21.6 million.
 Following the sale of its final vessel, DDW Offshore has entered a run-off
 phase with no remaining vessel operations.
* Net Asset Value was NOK 4.3 billion at the end of the quarter, corresponding
 to NOK 15.7 per share.
CEO Karl Erik Kjelstad comments:
"The developments during and after the third quarter demonstrate continued
progress in Akastor's transition from value creation to value realisation. The
NOK 2.50 per share dividend announced today brings total distributions since
July 2025 to approximately NOK 1.5 billion, corresponding to NOK 5.65 per
share, and reflects our ambition to return capital as portfolio values are
realised.
We continue to see significant value in our remaining portfolio. While HMH's
third-quarter performance and subsequent share price development have been
disappointing, our view of its longer-term potential has not changed. We also
see attractive opportunities for further value realisation across our key
holdings and, with a strong financial position, we have the flexibility to
optimise for value while continuing to pursue realisations and return excess
capital to shareholders."
HMH
HMH reported revenue of USD 171 million in the third quarter, down 21%
year-on-year, while adjusted EBITDA amounted to USD 38 million, corresponding
to an adjusted EBITDA margin of 22%. Orders amounted to USD 191 million, up
12% year-on-year and resulting in a book-to-bill ratio of 1.12x.
Equipment order activity remained below expectations during the quarter, with
several larger equipment and upgrade opportunities shifting to later periods
and customer contract awards taking longer than anticipated. HMH has stated
that these opportunities have not disappeared and that the company continues
to see a healthy pipeline across its installed base. HMH also remains
confident in the underlying deepwater fundamentals and believes it is well
positioned for opportunities developing into 2027.
HMH completed the acquisition of Deepwater Riser Services in September for USD
14.5 million, expanding its riser inspection, recertification, refurbishment
and storage capabilities in the U.S. Gulf.
Further details on HMH's third quarter 2026 financial results are available
through HMH's investor relations website and its Quarterly Report on Form
10-Q.
AKOFS Offshore
AKOFS Offshore reported revenues of USD 46 million and EBITDA of USD 19
million in the quarter, driven by strong operational performance across the
fleet, with revenue utilisation of 99% for Aker Wayfarer, 97% for AKOFS Santos
and 96% for AKOFS Seafarer.
During the quarter, AKOFS completed a USD 300 million fleet refinancing and
exercised the purchase option for Aker Wayfarer, strengthening its long-term
funding and securing ownership of a core operating asset.
Post quarter-end, AKOFS Santos entered the yard for planned upgrades ahead of
commencement of its new Petrobras contract in the first quarter of 2027.
DDW Offshore
DDW Offshore reported revenue of NOK 34 million and EBITDA of NOK 11 million
in the third quarter. Skandi Peregrino remained on contract in Australia until
late September, delivering 91% utilisation during the quarter.
Post quarter-end, the sale of Skandi Peregrino was completed for USD 21.6
million. Following the sale of its final vessel, DDW Offshore has entered a
run-off phase with no remaining vessel operations.
Financial holdings
Net financial items were negative NOK 41 million in the quarter, primarily
reflecting non cash foreign exchange effects, partly offset by contributions
from financial investments and net interest.
Net profit from equity accounted investments was NOK 10 million in the period,
of which HMH contributed NOK 14 million (non cash for Akastor).
Consolidated financial figures
Please note that Akastor's consolidated revenue and EBITDA include earnings
from subsidiaries, which represent a limited portion of the company's
underlying portfolio values. As such, the most relevant indicator of value
development remains the financial performance of Akastor's key investments.
On this basis, Akastor reported consolidated revenues of NOK 35 million and
EBITDA of negative NOK 7 million in the quarter, while net loss amounted to
NOK 16 million.

title: Akastor ASA: Resultat for tredje kvartal 2026
body:
Høydepunkter fra tredje kvartal
* Utbytte på NOK 2,50 per aksje vedtatt, basert på kontantutbetaling fra NES
 Fircroft og salget av Skandi Peregrino i oktober.
* Med dette utgjør samlede utdelinger siden juli 2025 om lag NOK 1,5
 milliarder, tilsvarende NOK 5,65 per aksje.
* HMH leverte justert EBITDA på USD 38 millioner med en margin på 22 prosent.
 Ordreinngang innen segmentet Products var lavere enn forventet, med flere
 prosesser skjøvet ut i tid. HMH har fortsatt tro på de underliggende
 markedsforholdene innen offshore boring.
* AKOFS Offshore hadde solid operasjonell drift på tvers av flåten og
 gjennomførte en refinansiering på USD 300 millioner, som sikrer langsiktig
 finansiering og eierskap til Aker Wayfarer.
* Etter kvartalsslutt mottok Akastor USD 57,4 millioner etter refinansiering
 og påfølgende rekapitalisering av NES Fircroft.

 Etter salget av sitt siste fartøy har DDW Offshore ingen gjenværende
 operasjonell drift.
* Nettoverdijustert egenkapital (NAV) var NOK 4,3 milliarder ved utgangen av
 kvartalet, tilsvarende NOK 15,7 per aksje.
Akastor CEO Karl Erik Kjelstad kommenterer:
"Akastor fortsetter å ta viktige steg fra verdiskaping til verdirealisering.
Utbyttet på NOK 2,50 per aksje som annonseres i dag, gir en samlet utbetaling
siden juli 2025 på om lag NOK 1,5 milliarder, tilsvarende NOK 5,65 per aksje,
og reflekterer vår ambisjon om å tilbakeføre kapital til aksjonærene etter
hvert som investeringer realiseres.
Vi ser fortsatt betydelige verdier i den gjenværende porteføljen. Selv om HMHs
resultatutvikling i tredje kvartal og den påfølgende aksjekursutviklingen har
vært skuffende, er vårt syn på selskapets langsiktige potensial uendret. Vi
ser også attraktive muligheter for videre verdirealisering på tvers av våre
viktigste investeringer, og med en sterk finansiell posisjon har vi
fleksibilitet til å optimalisere for verdi samtidig som vi fortsetter arbeidet
med realiseringer og tilbakeføring av kapital til aksjonærene."

se engelsk versjon av børsmeldingen.

title: ENVIPCO Q3 26 - Rising sales growth and record customer awards
body:
Q3 26 highlights:
- Group revenues EUR 26.5m, up 18% y/y on stronger US RVM sales and higher
Europe program services
- Gross margin of 33.1%, continuing to reflect investments in service teams
and underutilization in assembly operations
- EBITDA EUR -0.6m and operating profit at EUR -3.1m on sequentially higher
gross margin and lower opex
- Strong commercial traction largely driven by 7,100 RVM committed orders in
the UK to date
Subsequent events
- On 28 October Envipco was announced as exclusive supplier to a major UK
retailer for delivery of approximately 1,700 Compact, Flex, Optima and Magna
RVMs from Q1 27
- In November, Envipco entered into an asset financing agreement for RVMs on
throughput contract providing liquidity of EUR 8m for existing contracts
Amersfoort, The Netherlands, 11 November 2026 - Envipco Holding N.V.
("Envipco" or "the Company"), a leading global provider of recycling systems
and Reverse Vending Machine (RVM) technology, reported rising sales growth in
Q3 26 with revenues up 18% y/y to EUR 26.5m driven by higher RVM revenues from
North America and growth in European program services.
"We remain committed to our communicated strategy. We are strengthening our
execution and creating a more agile and responsive organization to convert
opportunities into profitable growth. This includes building one global
commercial organization, reallocating selected resources to where demand is
building and refining business processes" says CEO José Matthijsse.
On a product line basis, RVM revenues increased 17% to EUR 15.3m on higher
sales in North America, while program service revenues were a record EUR
11.2m, up 19% on growth in Europe.
Geographically, Europe saw a 7% revenue increase to EUR 15.2m, with recurring
program revenue up 91% to EUR 3.4m. North America delivered record revenues of
EUR 11.3m, up 37%.
Gross margin was 33.1% compared to 35.0% in Q3 25 and up from 32.2% in Q2 26,
with the level continuing to reflect low capacity utilization in assembly
operations and building of service organizations in new markets. Gross profit
for the quarter ended at EUR 8.8m, up from EUR 7.9m in the third quarter last
year.
Operating expenses amounted to EUR 11.9m in the third quarter, up 13% y/y but
down sequentially from EUR 12.1m in Q2 26, with the y/y increase mainly
reflecting higher headcount and professional fees as part of key improvement
projects. EBITDA for the third quarter of 2026 ended at EUR -0.6m, compared to
an EBITDA of EUR -0.3m in Q3 25, with operating profit of EUR -3.1m compared
to EUR -2.7m in Q3 25.
Outlook:
Envipco is experiencing market tailwinds as DRS is being mandated across the
EU on approved regulation and enacted DRS legislation. Several European
markets are in process of launching, or expected to launch, their deposit
return systems in the years to come, which could triple the company's total
addressable market.
The company's US operations are expected to remain stable with some growth in
RVM sales from new RVM orders. In Europe Envipco has secured Romanian orders
for 2027 deliveries, building into the long-tail of the market. The company is
delivering on its Portugal wins and continues to develop the broader market.
Envipco is sharpening its commercial approach in Poland. The Netherlands
remains a dynamic and promising opportunity for the company and the frame
agreement with the DRS operator has been extended through 2027.
The UK represents the largest commercial driver for Envipco from 2027. Envipco
has established a strong initial market position with secured wins for 7,100
RVMs in addition to a preferred supplier agreement offering additional sales
potential. Envipco remains heavily engaged to secure its target share in the
UK market.
Greece is progressing towards launching national DRS with DRS Hellas recently
appointed as DMO for a 5-year term. Envipco is actively positioning towards
this market opportunity together with its local distributor.
The initiatives to strengthen the company's execution and create a more agile
and responsive organization result in some redundancies and the company
expects to incur EUR 3m restructuring charge in Q4 26, driving EUR 4m of
savings in 2027.
While continuing to invest in strategic priorities, Envipco will remain
focused on efficiency, capital allocation, and cash conversion. The company

title: Norconsult - Initiation of share buyback program
body:
Sandvika 11 November 2026 (OSE: NORCO): Norconsult ASA ("Norconsult" or the
"Company") announces the initiation of a share buyback program in accordance
with the authorization granted to the Board of Directors by the Annual General
Meeting of the Company held on 4 May 2026 ("the 2026 AGM").
The main purpose of the buyback program is to optimize the share capital
structure through a redemption of treasury shares by way of capital decrease,
which is considered to be beneficial for the Company's shareholders. Redemption
of shares will be subject to the general meeting's approval.
Norconsult may acquire shares for an aggregate consideration of up to NOK 100
million under the program. The maximum number of shares that can be acquired
under the program is 5.5 million. The minimum price that can be paid per share
is NOK 1 and the maximum price is NOK 200. The Company's holding of own shares
may, however, not at any point exceed 10% of the share capital pursuant to the
authorization granted by the 2026 AGM. The buyback program will commence on 11
November 2026 and will end no later than on 31 January 2027.
Norconsult has entered into a non-discretionary agreement with DNB Carnegie to
carry out the buyback program on its behalf. DNB Carnegie will make its trading
decisions independently of the Company. The execution of any repurchases will
depend on market conditions, and the Company may resolve to terminate the
buyback program before the thresholds set out above are reached. The Company
also reserves the right to make subsequent changes to the above terms for the
program and will in such case make appropriate announcements in this respect.
The buyback program will be carried out in accordance with the Market Abuse
Regulation (EU) No 596/2014 ("MAR") and Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) No
2016/1052 ("Safe Harbour Regulation").
This information is considered to be inside information pursuant to the EU
Market Abuse Regulation and is subject to the disclosure requirements pursuant
to Section 5-12 the Norwegian Securities Trading Act. This stock exchange
release was published by Elin Spieler, Head of Treasury and IR Manager,

Himalaya Shipping Ltd. (HSHP) Announces its Preliminary Results for the Three and Nine Months Ended September 30, 2026
body:
Hamilton, Bermuda, November 10, 2026
Himalaya Shipping Ltd. ("Himalaya," "Himalaya Shipping" or the "Company") announces preliminary unaudited results for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026.
Highlights for the Third Quarter of 2026
Total time charter revenues of $62.2 million, which represents average time charter equivalent ("TCE") earnings of approximately $58,400 per day, gross[1]. Average Baltic 5TC 180 Capesize Index was $41,369 per day.
Net income of $33.3 million and EBITDA[2] of $52.7 million.
Entered into a new time charter agreement for the Mount Aconcagua for a period of 16 to 18 months at an index-linked rate, reflecting a significant premium to the Baltic 5TC 180 Capesize Index.
Converted the index-linked time charters for two vessels to fixed-rate time charters at an average rate of approximately $51,200 per day, gross, from August 1, 2026 to December 31, 2026.
Converted the index-linked time charters for two vessels to fixed-rate time charters at an average rate of approximately $53,000 per day, gross, from September 1, 2026 to March 31, 2027.
Paid cash distributions of $0.22, $0.25 and $0.28 per common share for July, August and September 2026, respectively
Subsequent Events
Achieved TCE earnings for October 2026 of approximately $50,900 per day, gross.
Declared a cash dividend of $0.20 per common share for October 2026.
Acquired an additional 1,800 shares in Peak Maritime for NOK 0.5 million, increasing the Company's total ownership in Peak Maritime to 60%.
Entered into new time charter agreements with their existing charterer for two vessels for a minimum period until October 1, 2027 with a 3-year evergreen structure thereafter at an index-linked rate, reflecting a significant premium to the Baltic 5TC 180 Capesize Index.
Himalaya Shipping Ltd. is an independent bulk carrier company, incorporated in Bermuda. Himalaya Shipping has twelve vessels in operation.
November 10, 2026
The Board of Directors
Himalaya Shipping Ltd.
Hamilton, Bermuda
[1] The Company uses certain financial information calculated on a basis other than in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States (US GAAP) including average TCE earnings, gross and EBITDA. ATHENS, GREECE, November 11, 2026 - Okeanis Eco Tankers Corp. Financial performance of the Third Quarter Ended September 30, 2026
 - Revenues of $501.5 million in Q3 2026, compared to $90.6 million in Q3 2025.
 - Profit of $299.6 million in Q3 2026, compared to $24.1 million in Q3 2025.
 - Vessel operating expenses of $14.8 million in Q3 2026, compared to $11.7 million in Q3 2025.
 - Earnings per share of $7.67 in Q3 2026, compared to $0.75 in Q3 2025.
 - Cash (including restricted cash) of $233.1 million as of September 30, 2026, compared to $122.5 million as of December 31, 2025.
Financial performance of the Nine Months Ended September 30, 2026
 - Revenues of $990.5 million in 9M 2026, compared to $264.7 million in 9M 2025.
 - Profit of $618.2 million in 9M 2026, compared to $63.5 million in 9M 2025.
 - Vessel operating expenses of $40.4 million in 9M 2026, compared to $33.8 million in 9M 2025.
 - Earnings per share of $15.95 in 9M 2026, compared to $1.97 in 9M 2025.
Alternative performance metrics and market development
 - Time charter equivalent* ("TCE", a non-IFRS measure*) revenue of $338.3 million in Q3 2026.
 - EBITDA* and Adjusted EBITDA* (each, a non-IFRS measure*) of $323.1 million and $320.4 million, respectively, in Q3 2026.
 - Adjusted profit* and Adjusted earnings per share* (each, a non-IFRS measure*) of $299.5 million or $7.67 per basic and diluted share in Q3 2026.
 - During Q3 2026, we entered into a series of short-term charter agreements for five of our VLCC vessels, for a period of 100-150 days each, with an average rate of $449,200 per day.
 - In Q3 2026, fleetwide daily TCE rate* of $206,800 per available spot day and $209,100 per operating day; VLCC TCE rate of $269,300 per available spot day and $260,100 per operating day; and Suezmax TCE rate of $166,600 per available spot and operating day.
 - Daily vessel operating expenses* ("Daily Opex", a non-IFRS measure*) of $9,401 per calendar day, in Q3 2026.
 - In Q4 2026 to date: on the VLCC fleet 48% of the available spot days have been booked at an average TCE rate of $688,800 per day and 87% of operating days have been booked at an average TCE rate of $430,300; on the Suezmax fleet 60% of available spot and operating days have been booked at an average TCE rate of $410,900.
Declaration of Q3 2026 dividend

title: Endúr ASA - Acquisition of Romarheim Entreprenør
body:
12 November 2026 - Endúr ASA ("Endúr") is happy to announce its planned acquisition of 100% of the shares in Romarheim Entreprenør AS, including its subsidiaries ("Romarheim"/"The Company").
Romarheim is a civil contractor undertaking complex construction projects within energy, infrastructure and industry. The Company specializes in groundworks, water and sewage infrastructure, drilling, blasting and mass handling for projects such as transformer stations, power grids, hydropower facilities, roads and tunnels. Based in Alversund outside Bergen, Norway, The Company has a workforce of approximately 125 people. The acquisition further strengthens Endúr's infrastructure investment strategy by adding a strong, proactive project organization, new market positions and complementary geographical coverage. Romarheim will join as a new platform company and part of Endúr's Rehabilitation & Intersections segment.
Trygve Andås, General Manager of Romarheim, and other key employee shareholders will remain in their current positions and become shareholders in Endúr through consideration shares issued as part of the transaction settlement. The Company will retain its workforce, brand, premises and business model, with full continuity in its customer and supplier relationships. At the same time, the acquisition is expected to create attractive opportunities for project collaboration with Endúr's other platform companies, while The Company will continue to operate as an independent and autonomous entity.
"Romarheim stood out as a high-priority acquisition target, providing an attractive service offering, project portfolio and market exposure, driven by a front-footed and commercially oriented management and organization with a proven track record for creating rapid growth and strong profitability", says Jeppe Raaholt, CEO of Endúr. 
The acquisition values The Company at a base enterprise value on a cash- and debt-free basis, excluding leasing liabilities ("Base EV"), of NOK 700 million. The Company's projected consolidated FY 2026 revenues are approximately NOK 1,100 million (FY 2025: NOK 933 million), with an operating result ("EBIT") of approximately NOK 102.5 million (FY 2025: NOK 81 million) and a margin of approximately 9.3% (FY 2025: 8.7%). The Base EV implies an EV/EBIT multiple of approximately 6.8x against a target average annual EBIT of NOK 102.5 million for the period 2026-2028. The acquisition adds approximately NOK 900 million to Endúr's existing backlog.
The Base EV may be adjusted upwards by up to NOK 200 million or downwards by up to NOK 135 million ("The Additional Consideration"), to be settled by 30 June 2029. Within these limits, The Additional Consideration will be calculated as the difference between average annual EBIT for FY 2026-2028 and a target of NOK 102.5 million, multiplied by 7.0x. The adjustment mechanism provides multiple protection for average annual EBIT during FY 2026-2028 in the approximate range of NOK 83-131 million.
The acquisition will be partly financed with a NOK 135 million seller's credit, to be settled by 30 June 2029 and offsettable against any negative Additional Consideration. The sellers will also receive consideration shares in Endúr valued at NOK 247.5 million, based on a 15-trading-day volume weighted average price ("VWAP") on the Oslo Stock Exchange, leading up to this announcement. The consideration shares will be subject to lock-up restrictions, with one-third released at each of 12, 18 and 24 months after closing.
"We look forward to continue developing Romarheim together with Endúr. With our significant ambitions for sustained growth and an expansion, Endúr stood out as a particularly attractive partner for the next stage of our journey", says Trygve Andås, General Manager of Romarheim.
A signed share purchase agreement ("SPA") is in place and the acquisition is expected to close by the end of this year's last quarter, with completion subject to approval from The Norwegian Competition Authority (No: "Konkurransetilsynet") and certain other customary conditions. 
Endúr was assisted by Danske Bank and EY as financial advisors and Wikborg Rein as legal advisor.

Endúr ASA (XOSL: ENDUR) is a leading Scandinavian contractor headquartered in Lysaker and listed on the Oslo Stock Exchange. The company specializes in critical infrastructure, including bridges, quays, tunnels, and dams. Operating as a disciplined serial acquirer (compounder), the group utilizes a decentralized model that grants subsidiaries high autonomy to preserve their technical expertise and local market positions. Endúr drives long-term value through strategic platform acquisitions and targeted bolt-ons in fragmented niche markets.

title: General Oceans ASA - Revenue growth of 13 percent in Q3 2026
body:
Oslo, 12 November 2026: General Oceans reports total revenue in Q3 2026 of NOK 320 million, an increase of 13 percent compared to Q3 2025 and a growth of 19 percent on a constant currency basis. Gross profits were NOK 206 million (NOK 197 million), corresponding to a gross margin of 64 percent (70 percent).
Adjusted EBITA in Q3 2026 was NOK 43 million compared to NOK 49 million in Q3 2025. EBITA in Q3 2026 is adjusted for NOK 8 million in one-time effects. Adjusted EBITA for the first three quarters is NOK 186 million (18% margin) compared to NOK 188 million (20% margin) in the first nine months of 2025.
The defense market continues to grow, and defense revenue for the first nine months was NOK 386 million, up 43 percent from NOK 269 million last year. In contrast, the offshore wind market is characterised by higher development costs, higher financing costs and political headwinds. As a result, revenue from the Marine Construction market is down almost 10 percent over the same period. Sales volumes to the Ocean Science market are holding steady, with revenue up 10 percent year to date including MRV.
"We continue to grow our defense business. Simultaneously, our response to the more challenging market and FX environment is an increased focus on delivering new products, allocating sales effort where it produces the most value and closer alignment between the operating companies and our overall goals," said Atle Lohrmann, President of General Oceans ASA.
Order backlog as at 30 September 2026 was NOK 518 million and order intake during Q3 2026 was NOK 293 million.

title: Endúr ASA - Q3 2026 financial results
category: ADDITIONAL REGULATED INFORMATION REQUIRED TO BE DISCLOSED UNDER THE LAWS OF A MEMBER STATE
body:
12 November 2026 - Endúr ASA (Endúr) continued its positive development in the third quarter of 2026, delivering growth in both revenues and operating results. Revenue increased 8 percent to NOK 1,996.5 million, from NOK 1,841.6 million in the same period last year. EBITA increased 29 percent to an all-time high NOK 170.2 million (132.0), equivalent to a margin of 8.5 percent (7.2). 
"The third quarter marked a new quarterly earnings record for Endúr, with all-time high EBITA and EBITA margin, driven particularly by strong performance in our infrastructure businesses. We maintained high production activity, continued to pursue strategic growth opportunities through acquisitions and secured increased financial flexibility through a corresponding refinancing", says Jeppe Raaholt, CEO of Endúr.
Cash flow from operating activities was NOK 207.4 million in the third quarter. Net working capital remained relatively stable, following the increase recorded in the first half of the year. Endúr's cash balance was NOK 606 million at quarter-end, while total available liquidity amounted to NOK 1,156 million including the NOK 550 million unused overdraft facility.
The group recorded order intake of NOK 820 million in the quarter, bringing the order backlog to NOK 7.7 billion at the end of September 2026. The backlog includes NOK 1.84 billion scheduled for the remainder of 2026 and NOK 3.61 billion for 2027. In addition, the group continues to benefit from substantial recurring and framework-based revenues not fully reflected in backlog figures.
BUSINESS SEGMENT UPDATE
Revenue in Rehabilitation & Intersections was NOK 733.4 million in the third quarter (599.4), representing growth of 22 percent. EBITA increased 79 percent to NOK 90.9 million (50.8), corresponding to an EBITA margin of 12.4 percent (8.5). The segment recorded NOK 275 million in order intake during the quarter and had an order backlog of NOK 2.4 billion at quarter-end. During the quarter, the acquisition of Wimo was completed, strengthening BMO Fjell's specialist expertise and capabilities within rockfall and landslide protection.
Ports & Marine revenue increased 17 percent to NOK 483.7 million in the third quarter (413.5). EBITA was NOK 38.6 million (39.4), corresponding to an EBITA margin of 8.0 percent (9.5). The segment recorded NOK 275 million in order intake during the quarter and had an order backlog of NOK 1.65 billion. The Norwegian operations maintain a profitable backlog supported by strategic platform projects for the coming periods, while the segment remains focused on strengthening the backlog in Sweden, where the market remains healthy but less visible. During the quarter, the acquisition of Boston AS was completed.
Construction revenue was NOK 515.5 million in the third quarter (498.8), representing growth of 3 percent. EBITA increased to NOK 40.4 million (39.2), corresponding to an EBITA margin of 7.8 percent (7.9). The order backlog was NOK 3.08 billion, with NOK 175 million in order intake during the quarter. The segment has strong revenue coverage for the remainder of 2026 and continues to pursue promising industrial and property projects to improve backlog visibility for 2027.
Revenue in Aquaculture & Maritime Industry was NOK 272.3 million in the third quarter (331.0). EBITA decreased to NOK 12.8 million (15.0), corresponding to an EBITA margin of 4.7 percent (4.5). The decrease in EBITA was primarily attributable to lower revenues and earnings from ship maintenance activities following contractual discussions with the Norwegian Defence Materiel Agency (FMA), partly offset by contributions from land-based aquaculture projects. The segment had an order backlog of NOK 600 million at quarter-end and is awaiting clarification on several potential projects, including Salfjord, which is not included in the reported backlog pending a final investment decision.
OUTLOOK
Endúr continues to experience high tender activity and a large volume of outstanding bids across its core markets. The group has strong backlog coverage for the remainder of 2026 and continues to focus on strengthening longer-term backlog visibility.
Future activity is supported by the Norwegian National Transport Plan for 2025-2036, which favours rehabilitation and smaller infrastructure projects. Increased defence spending, favourable market conditions within selected real estate and construction markets and the general maintenance gap on critical infrastructure are also expected to support future activity. Endúr is also expanding its position within the data centre market through Avendur Nordic, providing exposure to a market with growing investment demand.
Within Aquaculture & Maritime Industry, ongoing land-based aquaculture projects continue to support near-term activity, while longer-term revenue coverage and utilisation of engineering capacity remain areas of focus. The segment is awaiting clarification on several potential projects and remains focused on strengthening longer-term backlog coverage and improving the utilisation of engineering capacity.
Endúr will continue to focus on profitable growth through operational improvements, organic investments and targeted M&A activities. Following several completed and announced acquisitions during 2026, the group maintains an active pipeline of potential structural investments and financial flexibility to support continued growth.

title: NORBIT - Resultater for tredje kvartal 2026
body:
Trondheim, 12. november 2026: NORBIT leverte i tredje kvartal en omsetning på
676,7 millioner kroner, en økning på 34 prosent sammenlignet med tilsvarende
kvartal i 2025. Driftsresultatet (EBIT) økte med 53 prosent til 115,5 millioner
kroner, fra 75,4 millioner kroner i samme periode i 2025. Utvannet resultat per
aksje var 1,12 kroner i tredje kvartal, opp fra 0,81 kroner året før.
 * Oceans bidro med en omsetning på 260,6 millioner kroner, en økning på 35
 prosent fra samme kvartal i 2025, med en EBIT-margin på 29 prosent.
 Oppkjøpet av 100 prosent av aksjene i Water Linked ble gjennomført 1. juli.
 * Connectivity rapporterte en omsetning på 148,3 millioner kroner, en økning
 på 38 prosent fra tredje kvartal 2025, med en EBIT-margin på 15 prosent.
 Connectivity inngikk i kvartalet en avtale med Toll4Europe til en verdi av
 om lag 325 millioner kroner. Leveransene er planlagt å starte mot slutten av
 fjerde kvartal 2026, med hoveddelen i 2027.
 * Product Innovation & Realization (PIR) leverte en omsetning på 286,2
 millioner kroner, en økning på 28 prosent, med en EBIT-margin på 16 prosent.
"Alle forretningssegmentene bidro til vekst i kvartalet, noe som viser styrken
og robustheten i vår forretningsmodell med diversifiserte virksomhetsområder. Vi
setter stor pris på tilliten kundene viser oss og på alle våre medarbeideres
solide innsats og engasjement", sier Per Jørgen Weisethaunet, konsernsjef i
NORBIT.
Med bakgrunn i NORBITs solide balanse og finansielle stilling har styret vedtatt
et tilleggsutbytte på 2,00 kroner per aksje for regnskapsåret 2025. Samlet
utbytte for 2025 blir dermed 7,00 kroner per aksje.
Utsiktene for fjerde kvartal er gode, og NORBIT forventer en omsetning for 2026
på mellom 3,0 og 3,1 milliarder kroner og en EBIT-margin på mellom 21 og 22
prosent inkludert bidraget fra Water Linked og tilhørende transaksjonskostnader
knyttet til oppkjøpet.
"Godt inne i årets siste kvartal, som vanligvis er vårt travleste, opplever vi
høy aktivitet i hele konsernet. Positive underliggende drivere i markedene våre,
kombinert med NORBITs økende størrelse og kapasitet, gir oss muligheter til å
styrke vår posisjon innenfor de vertikalene vi opererer i.
Vår vertikalt integrerte forretningsmodell er bygd på dyktige
utviklingsingeniører, egen industriell produksjonskompetanse og -kapasitet samt
inngående domenekunnskap som vi kontinuerlig akkumulerer gjennom tett dialog med
kunder over hele verden. Fortsatte investeringer i kapasitet og folk forsterker
vår evne til å møte kundebehov i større skala.
Vår strategiske prioritet er å utnytte disse kapasitetene til å levere på
vekststrategien vår: broaden our product offering og expand our customer base.
Dette gjennom markedsdrevet innovasjon, der vi tilbyr tailored technology to
carefully selected applications. Vi erfarer at vedvarende vekst og økt skala i
virksomheten gjør oss relevante for en utvidet kundebase og setter oss i stand
til å gripe et bredere spekter av muligheter. Dette skaper nye muligheter til å
Explore More", sier Per Jørgen Weisethaunet, konsernsjef i NORBIT.

title: NORBIT - Results for the third quarter of 2026
body:
Trondheim, 12 November 2026: In the third quarter, NORBIT recorded revenues of
NOK 676.7 million, an increase of 34 per cent from the corresponding quarter of
2025. Operating profit (EBIT) increased by 53 per cent to NOK 115.5 million,
from NOK 75.4 million in the corresponding period of 2025. Diluted earnings per
share were NOK 1.12 for the third quarter, up from NOK 0.81 one year earlier.
 * The Oceans segment delivered revenues of NOK 260.6 million, an increase of
 35 per cent from the same quarter of 2025, with an EBIT margin of 29 per
 cent. The acquisition of 100 per cent of the shares in Water Linked was
 completed 1 July.
 * The Connectivity segment reported NOK 148.3 million in revenues, an increase
 of 38 per cent from the third quarter of 2025, and an EBIT margin of 15 per
 cent.
 The Connectivity segment entered into an agreement with Toll4Europe worth
 approximately NOK 325 million. Deliveries are scheduled to commence towards
 the end of Q4 2026, with the majority taking place in 2027.
 * The Product Innovation & Realization (PIR) segment saw revenues of NOK
 286.2 million, representing an increase of 28 per cent, with an EBIT margin
 of 16 per cent.
"All segments contributed to growth in the quarter, demonstrating the strength
and resilience of our diversified business model. We are grateful for the
continued trust of our customers and the commitment of all our colleagues," says
Per Jørgen Weisethaunet, CEO of NORBIT.
Due to the strong balance sheet and financial position of NORBIT, the board of
directors decided to resolve an additional dividend of NOK 2.00 per share based
on the financial year 2025, bringing the total dividend to NOK 7.00 per share
for the said year.
The outlook for the fourth quarter is solid, and NORBIT expects full-year
revenues in the range of NOK 3.0 - 3.1 billion, and an EBIT margin of 21 - 22
per cent for 2026, including contribution and the related transaction costs from
the latest acquisition Water Linked.
"Well into the final quarter of the year, typically our busiest, we are
experiencing strong momentum across the group. Positive underlying drivers
across our markets, combined with NORBIT's increasing scale, are creating
opportunities to strengthen our position in the verticals we serve.
Our vertically integrated business model brings together skilled R&D engineers,
in-house industrial manufacturing capabilities and deep domain knowledge,
continuously developed through close dialogue with customers around the world.
Continued investments in capacity and people further strengthen our ability to
address customer needs on a larger scale.
Our strategic priority is to leverage these capabilities to deliver on our
growth strategy: broaden our product offering and expand our customer base
through market-driven innovation, bringing tailored technology to carefully
selected applications. We are experiencing that our continued growth and the
increased scale of our operations make us relevant to a broader customer base
and position us to pursue a wider range of opportunities, creating new
possibilities to Explore More," says Per Jørgen Weisethaunet, CEO of NORBIT.

title: Veidekke: Q3 2026 results
body:
Veidekke achieved revenue of NOK 11.8 billion in the third quarter, and a pre
-tax profit of NOK 904 million. The quarterly order intake totalled NOK 8.3
billion and brought the group's order book to NOK 52.6 billion at quarter-end.
"Veidekke has had a strong third quarter, with both revenue and profit up year
-on-year. Activity levels are high, capacity utilisation is good and margins are
robust across the project portfolio. The profit improvement in the quarter was
particularly strong in Norway, in both the construction and infrastructure
operations," says Group CEO Jimmy Bengtsson.
"Thanks to a robust order intake of NOK 8.3 billion in the quarter, the order
book remains at a high level. Orders due to be executed in the next 12 months
are 14 percent higher than a year ago, providing a solid starting point for
future activity," says Bengtsson.
Veidekke's quarterly revenue totalled NOK 11.8 billion, up 11 percent from NOK
10.7 billion in Q3 2025. Activity levels were up across all of Veidekke's
operations in the third quarter.
The third-quarter pre-tax profit amounted to NOK 904 million, up from NOK 721
million in Q3 2025. The profit improvement was mainly driven by increased
activity levels and better capacity utilisation, particularly in the Norwegian
operations. The PTP margin improved to 7.7 percent, up from 6.8 percent in Q3
2025.
The group's quarterly order intake was NOK 8.3 billion, compared to NOK 7.2
billion in the same period last year. At quarter-end, the order book amounted to
NOK 52.6 billion, compared to NOK 47.5 billion at the same time last year. Some
59 percent of the order book will be converted into revenue in the next 12
months.
The group's LTI rate (lost-time injuries per million hours worked) was 3.7 in
the third quarter, on par with the preceding quarter and down from 5.0 in Q3
2025. No serious injuries occurred during the quarter. The quarterly sick leave
rate was 4.2 percent, down from 4.7 percent in the preceding quarter and from
the same quarter last year.
The net interest-bearing position totalled NOK 4.9 billion as at 30 September
2026, compared to NOK 2.7 billion one year ago. Cash flow from operational
activities in the first three quarters of the year amounted to NOK 3.4 billion,
up from NOK 1.8 billion in the corresponding period in 2025. Total assets were
NOK 21.4 billion as at 30 September, up from NOK 19.0 billion at the same time
last year. The increase in total assets is primarily attributable to increased
activity levels.

title: Veidekke: Resultat for tredje kvartal 2026
body:
Veidekke omsatte for NOK 11,8 milliarder i tredje kvartal 2026. Resultatet før
skatt var NOK 904 millioner. Ordreinngangen i kvartalet var NOK 8,3 milliarder,
og ved utgangen av september hadde konsernet en ordrereserve på NOK 52,6
milliarder.
- Veidekke legger bak seg et sterkt tredje kvartal. Både omsetning og resultat
økte, sammenlignet med året før. Aktiviteten er høy, kapasitetsutnyttelsen er
god og det er solide marginer i prosjektporteføljen. Resultatforbedringen i
kvartalet var særlig sterk i Norge, både for bygg- og infrastrukturvirksomheten,
sier konsernsjef Jimmy Bengtsson.
- Med en solid ordreinngang i kvartalet på NOK 8,3 milliarder, ligger
ordrereserven på et fortsatt høyt nivå. Ordrer til utførelse i de neste 12
månedene er 14 % høyere enn for ett år siden, som gir et godt utgangspunkt for
aktiviteten fremover, sier Bengtsson.
Omsetningen i kvartalet utgjorde NOK 11,8 milliarder, en økning på 11 % fra NOK
10,7 milliarder i tredje kvartal 2025. Aktiviteten økte i samtlige av Veidekkes
virksomheter i tredje kvartal.
Resultatet i kvartalet var NOK 904 millioner, mot NOK 721 millioner i tredje
kvartal i fjor. Resultatforbedringen var hovedsakelig drevet av økt aktivitet og
bedre kapasitetsutnyttelse, spesielt i de norske virksomhetene. Resultatmarginen
økte til 7,7 %, fra 6,8 % året før.
Ordreinngangen i kvartalet var NOK 8,3 milliarder, mot NOK 7,2 milliarder i
samme periode i fjor. Ved utgangen av kvartalet var ordrereserven NOK 52,6
milliarder, mot NOK 47,5 milliarder året før. 59 % av ordrereserven kommer til
omsetning i de neste tolv månedene.
H1-verdi for konsernet (antall fraværsskader per million arbeidstimer) var 3,7 i
tredje kvartal, som er på samme nivå som i foregående kvartal, og ned fra 5,0 i
tredje kvartal 2025. Det var ingen alvorlige skader i tredje kvartal.
Sykefraværet i kvartalet utgjorde 4,2 %, ned fra 4,7 % i foregående kvartal og i
samme periode i fjor.
Netto rentebærende posisjon per 30. september var NOK 4,9 milliarder, mot NOK
2,7 milliarder året før. Kontantstrøm fra operasjonelle aktiviteter utgjorde NOK
3,4 milliarder hittil i år, mot NOK 1,8 milliarder i samme periode i fjor.
Balansen per 30. september var NOK 21,4 milliarder, en økning fra NOK 19,0
milliarder per tredje kvartal i fjor. Balanseøkningen tilskrives i hovedsak økt
aktivitet.

title: Energy Holdings: Seabird Exploration signs new contract for Fulmar Explorer
category: ADDITIONAL REGULATED INFORMATION REQUIRED TO BE DISCLOSED UNDER THE LAWS OF A MEMBER STATE
body:
Limassol, Cyprus -- 12 November, 2026 -- SeaBird Exploration, a wholly owned
subsidiary of SED Energy Holdings Plc ("Energy Holdings"), has been awarded a
contract for ocean bottom node (OBN) source work in West Africa. SeaBird will
deploy the Fulmar Explorer for the campaign. The total contract duration,
including mobilisation and demobilisation, is approximately six months, with
mobilisation expected to commence in December 2026.
Finn Atle Hamre, CEO of SeaBird Exploration, commented: " We are pleased to
secure another OBN source project for Fulmar Explorer, extending the vessel's
activity well into 2027. The award supports our view of an improving OBN
market, with increased tendering activity and better visibility for 2027. With
limited availability of relevant high-end tonnage, we believe SeaBird is well
positioned to capture further opportunities as market activity continues to
improve."

SED Energy Holdings Plc (ticker code "ENH") is a publicly listed investment
and holding company focused on building a portfolio of high-quality,
cash-generative businesses and assets within asset-based energy services.
Energy Holdings maintains a disciplined capital allocation strategy focused on
a conservative financial profile, returning excess capital to shareholders and
pursuing value-accretive growth opportunities. For more information, please
visit www.energyholdings.cy

Atea wins Microsoft's 2026 EMEA Regional Channel Partner of the Year award
body:
Microsoft recognized Atea for its work in creating business value for
organisations across both the private and public sectors through Microsoft
technology. This year's winners were selected from more than 4,500 nominations
worldwide.
- This recognition is first and foremost about our people and the value we
create together with customers every day. Technology is moving faster than ever,
particularly across AI and security. Our role is to make that change practical:
to help customers understand the opportunities, manage the risks and put
Microsoft technology to work in a secure and meaningful way. I am proud of what
all our teams have built together with Microsoft, and even more excited about
what we can help customers achieve next, says Carl-Johan Hultenheim, Chief
Operating Officer, Atea ASA.
First-hand experience that creates customer value
Atea helps customers create business value across the Microsoft technology
portfolio, drawing on the expertise of thousands of Atea consultants across
cloud, infrastructure, productivity, business applications, AI and security. For
Atea, being Customer Zero means putting the technology to work in its own
organization. The company became a Microsoft Frontier partner in June and has
rolled out the AI platform to all employees and created more than 14,000 AI
agents. This positions Atea to help customers achieve business outcomes with
Microsoft technology.
- Our certified specialists combine deep Microsoft expertise with practical
experience from our own organisation and years of working alongside customers.
That gives us a strong understanding of what it takes to choose the right
solutions, put them to work and build lasting value. We continue to develop our
expertise as the technology evolves, helping customers get more from their
Microsoft investments over time," says Carl-Johan Hultenheim, Chief Operating
Officer, Atea ASA.
Building cyber preparedness through hands-on practice
According to CIO Analytics 2026, 80 percent of organisations in Northern Europe
have an incident response plan, but only 24 percent practice regularly. To
address this, Atea, in collaboration with Microsoft, helps organisations
strengthen their cyber preparedness through Esc Room. The exercise takes place
inside a specially designed container, where participants experience a realistic
cyberattack based on real-world incidents. A debrief afterwards helps them
identify how to improve their response.
More than 4,500 nominations
The Microsoft Partner of the Year Awards celebrate partners delivering
exceptional customer outcomes through Microsoft Cloud, AI, services, and
devices. This year's winners and finalists were selected from more than 4,500
nominations submitted worldwide across a diverse range of categories and
geographies. Atea was recognized for providing outstanding solutions and
services as the Regional Channel Partner across Europe, the Middle East and
Africa.
- Congratulations to the winners and finalists of the 2026 Microsoft Partner of
the Year Awards. This year's honorees are harnessing the power of Microsoft
Cloud and AI to deliver transformative solutions, accelerate customer success,
and expand what's possible. Their ingenuity and impact inspire us, demonstrating
what can be achieved when bold vision and technology come together to empower
organizations around the world, said Nicole Dezen, Chief Partner Officer and
Corporate Vice President at Microsoft.
- Atea combines deep expertise across the Microsoft technology portfolio with a
strong understanding of customers' business needs. The company helps
organizations adopt technology, strengthen security and turn their investments
into business results. This award recognizes the value Atea helps customers
create, the expertise and commitment of Atea's people, and the strong
partnership across our both organizations", says Bart van der Knaap, Regional
Vice President EMEA Channel at Microsoft.
The 2026 Microsoft Partner of the Year Awards are announced ahead of Microsoft
Ignite, which will be held in San Francisco from November 17-20.
Additional details on the 2026 awards are available on the Microsoft Partner
blog: https://aka.ms/2026POTYA_Announcement. The complete list of categories,
winners and finalists can be found at https://aka.ms/2026POTYAWinnersFinalists.
For additional information, please contact:
Steinar Sønsteby, CEO Atea ASA, mobile (+47) 930 55 655

About Atea
Atea is the leading supplier of IT infrastructure in the Nordic and Baltic
regions. Atea is present in 88 cities with over 8,000 employees in Norway,
Sweden, Denmark, Finland, Lithuania, Latvia and Estonia. Atea delivers hardware
and software from leading global vendors, and provides consulting and technical
services to support its customers with the design, implementation and operation
of their IT environments. Atea had revenue of approximately NOK 37 billion (EUR
3.2 billion) in 2025 and is listed on Oslo Stock Exchange.
